zh: 第一章　破土
en: 1 Groundbreaking

zh: 在不久前的某个时刻，北大西洋世界的人们失去了时间感。他们开始把未来想象为一种无限资源，并以牺牲后来者为代价组织集体生活。奇怪的是，他们似乎始终意识到自己与未来的关系有缺陷。上个世纪的每一个十年都带来新的警告：资源枯竭、经济增长不可持续、地球遭受不可修复的损害。但他们主要把问题说成是计算失误。他们说，经济制度未能把自然考虑在内。在计算成本与收益时，它大体上排除了对自身之外的客体——自然世界——所造成的损害。如果他们确实在以未来为代价生活，那么这种占有似乎只是对地球的一种无意抽取。
en: Somewhere in the recent past, the people of the North Atlantic world lost their sense of time. They began to imagine the future as an infinite resource, and to organise collective life at the expense of those who would come later. Strangely, they always seemed aware that their relationship to the future was flawed. Every decade of the last century brought new warnings about the exhaustion of resources, unsustainable rates of economic growth, and irreparable damage to the Earth. But they framed the problem mainly as one of miscalculation. The economic system, they said, failed to take account of nature. In calculating costs and benefits, it largely excluded the damage done to an object outside themselves, the natural world. If they were living at the expense of the future, the appropriation seemed to happen as an inadvertent extraction from the Earth.

zh: 还有另一种方式，可以理解未来的生命和生活方式如何被弄得贫乏。未来的丧失并非计算失败的结果。我们生活在一套安排之中，这套安排被组织起来计算未来、确立其价值，并让某些人抽取和享有这种价值——不是在未来的某个时候，而是在当下。我们的生活方式并非忽视未来，而是朝向未来。但我们是以一种特定方式、通过特定的接触条件朝向它。同样，我们并不忽视物理和生物世界，而是通过具体的实践和理解与之发生关系。我们用自然、技术、经济、增长等术语来表达这种关系。这些词主要在二十世纪获得了当前的用法和含义，却使我们看不清自己如何以他人为代价生活。
en: There is a different way of understanding how future lives and ways of living are impoverished. The loss of the future is not the result of a failure to calculate. We live within a set of arrangements organised to calculate the future, establish its value, and allow some to extract and enjoy that value – not in a time to come, but in the present. Rather than neglecting the future, our mode of life is oriented towards it. But we are oriented in a particular manner, through specific terms of engagement. In the same way, we do not ignore the physical and biological world. But we relate to it through concrete practices and understandings. We express our relationship using terms like nature, technology, economy, and growth. Those words, which acquired their current use and meaning largely in the twentieth century, blind us to the way we live at the expense of others.

zh: 我们如何变得无法理解自己正以何种方式使地球变得不适合人类繁荣？我们如何发展出一些安排，使我们误认自己与未来的关系？要寻找答案，可以从回望二十世纪初开始。尽管关于自然世界、技术过程和经济力量的思考方式有更长的历史，但在上个世纪之交，新的政治和技术生活形式赋予这些观念不同的形态。这些生活形式产生于欧洲帝国扩张的顶点。正是在帝国的事件中，人们最清楚地看到它们出现。
en: How did we become uncomprehending of the ways in which we are rendering the Earth inhospitable to human flourishing? How did we develop arrangements that cause us to misrecognise our relationship to the future? To find answers, we can start by looking back to the beginning of the twentieth century. While ways of thinking about the natural world, technical processes, and economic forces have much longer histories, at the turn of the last century new forms of political and technical life gave such ideas a different shape. Those forms of life were produced at the high-water mark of European imperial expansion. It is in the events of empire that one can most clearly see them appear.

zh: 文明必须有其牺牲品
en: Civilisation Must Have Its Victims

zh: 1902 年，英国在埃及的水利工程师完成了毁灭尼罗河的第一阶段工程。埃及当时才被英国入侵和占领二十年。工程师们监督在开罗以南 500 英里的阿斯旺修建一座大坝，意在拦蓄河流夏季的大部分洪水。他们声称，目标是取代一种古老的灌溉方式：在围堤田块中蓄留洪水，每年只能种一季作物；代之以全年蓄水，实现常年灌溉，一年最多种植三季作物。把水蓄在大坝之后，可以消除异常洪水的威胁——洪水小时会导致作物歉收，极大时又会摧毁田地。调节河流不均衡的水流，也会减少因耕作面积不可预测而造成的财务不确定性。再加上把边缘土地纳入生产的新运河，扩大的耕作将能够养活不断增长的人口，同时让国家满足甘蔗和棉花等经济作物的需求。即使在今天，关于尼罗河的史书和埃及现代发展的叙述，仍在重复水利工程师带来的必要改良这一套说法。
en: In 1902, British hydraulic engineers in Egypt, a country Britain had invaded and occupied only two decades earlier, completed the first stage of the destruction of the River Nile. They supervised the building of a dam at Aswan, 500 miles south of Cairo, intended to hold back most of the river’s summer floodwaters. The aim, the engineers said, was to replace an ancient mode of irrigation based on capturing the flood in field basins, which allowed only a single crop each year, with year-round water storage that would allow perennial irrigation and the growing of up to three crops a year. Storing the water behind the dam would remove the threat of exceptional floods, which caused crops to fail when floods were low and devastated the fields when extremely high. Regulating the uneven flow of the river would also reduce the financial uncertainty caused by the unpredictable extent of cultivation. Combined with new canals bringing marginal lands into productive use, the expanded cultivation would enable the feeding of a growing population, while allowing the country to meet the demand for industrial crops like sugar cane and cotton. Even today, histories of the Nile and accounts of the country’s modern development repeat this narrative of necessary improvement introduced by the hydraulic engineers.

zh: 就像许多关于殖民现代性带来益处的叙述一样，这个故事几乎每一个要素都带有误导性或纯属错误。全年灌溉并没有用多季种植取代一年一季的作物，而几乎做了相反的事：用单一作物的大面积种植取代三季农业。灾难性干旱和洪水的风险，并不是新工程解决了的古老问题，而主要是灌溉工程

加剧的现代威胁。财务不确定性不是有待消除的不均衡，而是一种有待工程化制造的效果，以创造在当下从未来抽取支付的可能性。新工程没有把不毛之地纳入耕作，反而改变了边缘土地的使用方式，并使全国每一块田越来越不丰产，因为洪水、土壤形成、作物轮作、大型土壤动物和微生物生命之间的共生关系被扰乱和摧毁。大多数作物产量不升反降，因为洪水带来的淤泥不再肥田；只有一种植物例外，那就是水葫芦。这种原产亚马逊、能形成密集浮垫的水生杂草，由殖民时期的欧洲人作为观赏植物引入，它利用大坝造成的异常静水，逐渐用密集的草垫堵塞开罗以北的每条小运河和水道。洪水被消除后，人类本身变成了宿主，哺育不断扩张的寄生虫群体，包括携带钩虫病、疟疾和血吸虫病的寄生虫，而不是为不断增长的人口提供食物——随着粮食作物让位给棉花，人们的饮食已经恶化。但最具误导性的说法是那个主要说法：筑坝拦河通过全年蓄水消除了生态风险。英国人在阿斯旺建造的大坝和水库并未开创尼罗河水的储存。它们以不同方式储水，削弱并最终摧毁了一种规模更大、更为多样、却更不显眼的储水方式，以及管理气候、降雨和洪水不确定性的方式。
en: Like so many accounts of the benefits brought by colonial modernity, almost every element of that story is misleading or wrong. Year-round irrigation did not replace the growing of a single annual crop with multiple cropping, but accomplished almost the reverse, replacing three-season agriculture with the widespread cultivation of a single crop. The risk of catastrophic droughts and floods was not an ancient problem solved by new engineering but mainly a modern threat

exacerbated by irrigation works. Financial uncertainty was not an unevenness to be removed but an effect to be engineered, to create the possibility of extracting in the present payments from the future. Rather than bringing unproductive lands into cultivation, the new works altered the way marginal lands were used and rendered every field in the country less and less productive, as the symbiosis of flood, soil formation, crop rotation, macrofauna, and microbial life was disrupted and destroyed. Rather than increasing in yield, most crops declined, as the flood-borne silt no longer fertilised the land, with the exception of one plant, water hyacinth, a mat-forming aquatic weed from the Amazon introduced as a garden ornament by colonial Europeans, which took advantage of the unusually still waters created by the dam to gradually clog with dense matting every small canal and waterway north of Cairo. Rather than providing food for a growing human population, whose diet had worsened as food crops gave way to cotton, the elimination of the flood turned humans themselves into hosts, feeding an expanding population of parasites including those carrying hookworm disease, malaria, and bilharzia. But the most misleading claim is the main one, that damming up the river eliminated ecological risk by introducing the year-round storing of its waters. The dam and reservoir that the British built at Aswan did not initiate the storage of the waters of the Nile. They stored them differently, reducing and eventually destroying a much larger, more diverse, but less visible means of storing water and managing the uncertainties of climate, rainfall, and flood.

zh: 其中一些负面后果早已被承认，尽管通常被视为不可避免的副作用。“文明，”负责管理英国占领事务、并赞颂金融家与其“强大盟友”水利工程师合作的克罗默勋爵说，“不幸必须有其牺牲品。”

然而，没有现代叙述解释先前围堤田块的储水系统——以及我们将发现的、这些田块之下的系统——如何运作，或它如何被摧毁。要了解这一点，必须回到更早的文献，包括中世纪阿拉伯历史学家关于尼罗河农业的著述。现代叙述无法理解这条河的生态毁灭，部分原因在于它们参与了另一种世界观，而这一世界观正是由同样的事件塑造的。这种世界观基于另一种储存实践和另一种不确定性实践，形成与过去和未来不同的关系；这一差异对于建设殖民现代国家和实现现代资本主义致富具有根本意义。对尼罗河的
工程改造有助于产生一种与未来发生关系的新方式，这种方式后来被误认为“经济发展”。事实上，在水力工程史与金融史的一次不寻常交汇中，对尼罗河的毁灭在现代经济学及其误认我们以未来为代价的生活方式的有力方法的诞生中，扮演了一个次要却意味深长的角色。
en: Some of these negative consequences have long been recognised, although usually as unavoidable side effects. ‘Civilisation’, remarked Lord Cromer, the man who managed Britain’s occupation and celebrated the collaboration of the financier and his ‘powerful ally’, the hydraulic engineer, ‘must, unfortunately, have its victims.’

However, no modern account has explained the working of the previous system of water storage in field basins – and, as we will discover, beneath them – or how it was destroyed. For that one must turn back to earlier sources, including the writings of medieval Arab historians on the agriculture of the Nile. Part of the reason why modern accounts fail to understand the ecocide of the river is that they participate in another view of the world, a view shaped by the same events. That view is based on an alternative practice of storage, and an alternative practice of uncertainty, forming a different relation to past and future, a difference fundamental to building a colonial-modern state and modern capitalist enrichment. The

engineering of the Nile helped give rise to a novel way of relating to the future, one that came to be misrecognised as ‘economic development’. In fact, in an unusual intersection of the history of hydraulics and the history of finance, the destruction of the Nile played a minor but telling role in the very birth of modern economics and of its powerful method of misidentifying our mode of living at the expense of the future.

zh: 为了揭示生态毁灭与经济学之间、灌溉水流与现代金融流动之间的这些联系，让我们从大坝工程的不同之处开始。一个世界如何被组织起来，围绕着对未来的资本化而从中抽取收入——也就是在当下兑现那笔非劳动预期收入的能力？这种抽取，以及它所依赖的对大地的破坏和对生命的毁灭，如何通过经济学的诞生被误认并呈现为“资本主义”的“发展”？
en: To uncover these connections between ecocide and economics, between the flows of irrigation water and modern financial flows, let us start with what was different about the engineering of the dam. How was a world to be ordered around extraction from the future through its capitalisation, or the ability to realise that unearned prospective income in the present? How was this extraction, and the breaking of the earth and destruction of life on which it rested, misrecognised and presented, through the birth of economics, as the ‘development’ of ‘capitalism’?

zh: 耐久性
en: Durability

zh: 一切生命形式都在彼此互动、占用生存所需材料时，改变周围的元素。植物从土壤中吸收养分，同时又通过自身腐烂以及与所赖以为生的微生物互动，帮助创造土壤；线虫等土壤动物能改变根系结构、输送水分，并在土壤中制造隧道和通气孔；较大的动物消耗植物或其他动物，许多还用同样的材料建造住所。
收获蚁的巢穴会成为大型谷仓，它们把收集的种子储存在那里，从而为采食的植物传播种子，并因此改变当地生态。有些动物创造新的生态系统，例如河狸筑坝，或珊瑚建造水下礁体。人类也在做同样的事，初看之下尺度完全不同。
en: All forms of life modify the elements around them as they interact with one another and appropriate the materials they need to survive. Plants take nutrients from the soil, which in turn they help create, both through their own decay and through their interaction with the microbial life on which they feed; soil fauna such as nematodes (roundworms) can alter root structures, transport water, and manufacture tunnels and air passages through the soil; larger animals consume plants or other animals, and in many cases make shelters from the same materials.

The nests of harvester ants become large granaries, in which they store the seeds that they gather, providing seed dispersal for the plants from which they harvest, and thereby altering local ecologies. Some animals create new ecosystems, as with beavers constructing dams or corals manufacturing underwater reefs. Humans do the same, on what seems at first to be an altogether different scale.

zh: 人类建造和改造世界的物质总量令人震惊。仅大型水坝就重新分配了如此巨量的水，以至于建造它们改变了地球自转的速度和转轴。
被筑坝河流曾经输送的泥沙重量，如今与人类为修路、建房和采矿而移走的土石相比已微不足道。为破开地表、获取煤、铁矿石和其他资源而剥离的“覆盖层”，体量远超矿物本身，以
煤为例可达二十倍。据估计，这种人为泥沙搬运量是世界主要河流目前入海泥沙重量的二十四倍。
地质学家建议，把人类建造和改造生活世界所形成的地貌驱动力量，认定为地球的第五个圈层——与大气圈、水圈、岩石圈和生物圈这四个经典圈层并列——并提议称之为“技术圈”。
en: The mass of human construction and modification of the world is astonishing. Large dams alone have redistributed the volume of so much water that building them has changed the speed and axis of the Earth’s rotation.

The weight of sediment that dammed rivers once transported is now dwarfed by the human removal of earth and rock to construct roads and buildings and extract minerals. The ‘overburden’ removed to break apart the earth and access coal, iron ore, and other resources greatly exceeds the volume of the mineral itself, in the case of
coal by as much as twentyfold. This anthropogenic transport of sediment is estimated to be twenty-four times the weight of sediment the world’s major rivers now carry to the sea.

Geologists suggest we recognise the geomorphological driving force of human construction and modification of the lived world as the making of a fifth sphere of the Earth – alongside the four classical spheres of atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere – for which they propose the name ‘technosphere’.

zh: 技术圈指技术设备、人类社会性和物质生活的大规模安排，包括让能量、信息和物质流动的装置，涵盖发电站和输电网、道路和房屋、办公室和仓库、工业厂房和机床、煤田和油井、农场和商业渔场、种植园和经营林地，以及被筑坝和改道的大河水道。虽然“技术圈”一词让人想到工业和基础设施，但人类的大地改造主要发生在农业和林业中，二者合计已改造地球陆地面积的 38%，而建筑和基础设施仅占 1%。
一项初步估计认为，技术圈的质量可能高达 30 万亿吨。
据说人类自身的生物量约为 3 亿吨——这并非小数，约为所有野生陆生哺乳动物生物量的十二倍，尽管人类的总量又不及家畜——但它只占技术圈的极小部分。
按这些估计，技术圈的质量比人类生物量大五个数量级。人类建造或改造的城市、道路、房屋、工厂、运河、商业林、水坝、农田和重新工程化的洪泛平原系统，规模可能达到人类自身的十万倍。
en: The technosphere refers to the large-scale arrangements of technical equipment, human sociality, and material life, including the apparatuses that allow energy, information, and materials to flow, encompassing power stations and transmission grids, roads and houses, offices and warehouses, industrial plant and machine tools, coal fields and oil wells, farms and commercial fishing grounds, plantations and managed woodlands, and the dammed and rerouted channels of great rivers. While the word technosphere suggests industry and infrastructure, human terraforming occurs mainly in farming and forestry, which together have modified 38 per cent of the Earth’s land area, compared to 1 per cent occupied by buildings and infrastructure.
A preliminary estimate suggested that the mass of the technosphere might be as much as 30 trillion tonnes.

Humans themselves are said to have a biomass of about 300 million tonnes – no small figure, representing about twelve times the biomass of all wild terrestrial mammals, although humans are outweighed in turn by their domestic animals – but representing a miniscule part of the technosphere.

The mass of the technosphere, in these estimates, is five orders of magnitude larger than the human biomass. Humans have built or modified a system of cities, roads, houses, factories, canals, commercial forests, dams, farmland, and re-engineered floodplains that might be 100,000 times their own size.

zh: 然而更令人惊讶的，是技术圈的规模和质量，与我们最常用以把握其运作的那个极小术语之间——我们这样使用它不过大约七十五年——的差异：“经济”。我们习惯把经济视为一个宏观对象，类似于社会科学所描述的其他看似庞大的对象，如国家、社会、文化，甚至自然。经济自称是一种衡量和理解世界工业过程、基础设施、粮食系统、住房以及其他决定性人类物质生活方面的方式。但那种大规模之物的印象是误导性的。经济的出现，归功于支付、定价和
估算方式的传播，这些方式使得在定义和计量我们的物质存在时，可以把大部分技术生活和自然生活排除在考虑之外。正如我们后文将探讨的，经济是通过估算货币支付来衡量的，甚至不问支付机制如何建造，也不定位这些支付的资金在未来的何处被制造出来。与技术圈相比，我们不应把经济视为宏观对象，而应视为某种小得惊人的东西。
en: Still more astonishing, however, is the difference between the extent and mass of the technosphere and the miniscule term with which – for just the last seventy-five years or so – we most often try to grasp its workings: ‘the economy’. Conventionally we think of the economy as a macro-object, analogous to the other seemingly large objects that the social sciences describe, such as state, society, culture, and even nature. The economy purports to be a way of measuring and understanding the world’s industrial processes, infrastructures, food systems, housing, and other determining aspects of human material life. But the impression of something large-scale is misleading. The economy came into being thanks to the spread of modes of payment, pricing, and

estimating that made it possible to exclude most of technical and natural life from consideration in the definition and measurement of our material existence. The economy, as we will later explore, was measured by estimating monetary payments, without even asking how the mechanisms of payment were built or locating where in the future the funds for those payments were manufactured. In comparison to the technosphere, we should think of the economy not as a macro-object, but as something remarkably small.

zh: 其他试图把握人类对地球影响力量的术语，例如环境，也好不了多少。它们暗示一个被人类行动危及或试图管理的自然世界。但人类并非像“人类有机体及其环境”这一形象所暗示的那样，存在于技术圈之外。技术圈是由人类与非人类、生物与非生物、物质与政治要素混合而成的集合。
en: Other terms that try to capture the force of human impact on the Earth, such as the environment, are not much better. They imply a natural world that human action endangers or seeks to manage. But humans do not exist apart from the technosphere, as the image of a human organism and its environment suggests. The technosphere forms a mixed assembly of elements that are human and nonhuman, biotic and abiotic, material and political.

zh: 技术圈观念描绘的过程，远比我们作为“经济”来衡量的价格和交换系统庞大；但即使在此，仅关注其规模也可能误导我们。例如，在殖民时期的埃及，新大坝和灌溉工程主要作用于地表，忽视地表水、储存在土壤中的水，以及土壤和底土本身复杂生命形式之间的相互作用。技术圈质量的计算假定，农业中平均只有表层四到六英寸的土壤应被纳入测量。
技术圈只涉及“关键带”的一小部分；关键带是有生命与无生命交换的圈层，它涵盖并支撑各种生命形式，本身只是环绕地球表面的一层薄皮。
en: While the idea of the technosphere depicts processes that are much larger than the system of prices and exchanges that we measure as ‘the economy’, even here to focus on its scale can mislead us. In colonial Egypt, for example, the new dam and irrigation works operated mainly on the surface, ignoring the interaction between surface water, waters stored beneath the soil, and the complex life forms of the soil and subsoil itself. The calculation of the mass of the technosphere assumes that in agriculture on average only the top four to six inches of soil should be included in its measurement.

The technosphere refers only to a small part of the ‘critical zone’, the sphere of animate and inanimate exchanges that encompass and support forms of life, and itself a thin layer forming just a skin around the surface of planet Earth.

zh: 对我们理解从未来抽取的方式而言，人类技术圈最重要的不是其规模，而是另一种东西：其独特的耐久形式。其他生物对与之互动的元素所做的改变很少稳定：事物被消耗、腐烂、回归、转化或进一步发展。由此形成的物质循环——一个有机体的废物或腐烂为其他有机体提供养分——创造了自我维持的反馈循环，维持生命形式数百万年或数十亿年。
另一方面，技术圈的大部分由更稳定的组合装配而成，旨在减少与其他元素的交换，以抵抗老化、腐烂和物质再循环。它由各种安排和复合材料构成——例如混凝土、钢铁和塑料——往往能在数年或数十年内将
退化降至最低。这赋予技术圈一种独特的时间性。
en: Rather than its scale, what matters most in the human technosphere for our purpose of understanding modes of extraction from the future is something different: its peculiar form of durability. The modifications made by other organisms to the elements with which they interact are seldom stable: things are consumed, undergo decay, revert, transform, or develop further. The resulting recycling of materials, in which one organism’s waste or decay provides nourishment for others, creates self-sustaining feedback loops that have supported forms of life over millions or billions of years.

Much of the technosphere, on the other hand, is assembled out of more stable combinations, designed to reduce exchanges with other elements in order to resist ageing, decay, and recycling. It consists of arrangements and composites – concrete, steel, and plastics, for example – that often have the capacity to minimise
degeneration for years or decades. This gives the technosphere a distinctive temporality.

zh: 技术圈的很大一部分仅在过去 150 年间被生产或塑造出来，帮助定义了现代性的经验。这一变化在第一次世界大战前约两代人的时期尤为明显。
那些年间，钢铁和混凝土等复合材料的生产逐渐转变，其他材料及与之相关的机械也被引入，例如用于开凿运河的蒸汽铲、用于炸石和筑坝的炸药等烈性炸药、用于农业和弹药的合成化学品，以及蒸汽轮机；其钢制叶片使大规模发电成为可能，通过提供照明改变城市，并用电梯、电动有轨电车和轻轨系统使城市向上、向外扩张。
en: A large part of the technosphere has been produced or shaped in just the last 150 years, helping to define the experience of modernity. The change is particularly apparent in the period of roughly two generations before the First World War.

Those years saw a gradual shift in the production of composite materials such as steel and concrete, and the introduction of other materials and machinery associated with their use, such as steam shovels for excavating canals, high explosives like dynamite for rock blasting and dam construction, synthetic chemicals for use in agriculture and munitions, and the steam turbine, whose steel blades allowed the production of electric power at scale, transforming cities through the provision of lighting and expanding them upwards and outwards with electric elevators and electric-powered trams and light-rail systems.

zh: 新复合材料在技术圈独特的耐久性中发挥了显著作用。以钢为例。这种铁合金并非新材料，古人已知，数百年来用于制造需要耐久刃口或抗腐蚀的武器和工具。但从 1860 年代起，炼钢工艺的微小变化使其更便宜。直到 1865 年美国内战结束时，美国只有约 1% 的生铁（铸铁锭）被转化为钢；到 1906 年，转化率达到 100%。
钢随后在建设化石燃料系统（采矿和钻井设备、石油管道、炼油厂）、发电、化工厂、极高的钢架建筑、跨度空前的桥梁、“马克沁”自动装填机枪等武器、远洋航运和铁路中发挥关键作用。
en: The new composites played a noticeable role in the peculiar durability of the technosphere. Take the example of steel. This alloy of iron was not a new material, having been known to the ancients and used for centuries in making weapons and tools that required a durable blade or resistance to corrosion. But from the 1860s, minor changes in the steel-making process made it more affordable. As late as the end of the American Civil War, in 1865, only about 1 per cent of pig iron (the ingots of cast iron) in the United States was converted to steel; by 1906, the conversion rate was 100 per cent.

Steel then played a key part in building fossil fuel systems (mining and drilling equipment, oil pipelines, refineries), electrical power generation, chemical processing plants, steel-frame buildings of enormous height, bridges of unprecedented span, weaponry such as the Maxim self-loading machine gun, ocean-going shipping, and railways.

zh: 铁路线的建设在这一时期消耗的钢最多，也说明了这种耐久性的效果。在 1860 年代以前的早期蒸汽铁路时代，铁轨由熟铁制成；它比马拉铁路使用的易朽木轨能承载更重的交通，但在反复载荷下容易断裂，需要每六到十二个月更换，后来每三十六个月更换。铁轨断裂是火车事故的常见原因，检查和更换铁轨也是一项主要成本。1860 年代后改用钢轨，更换周期增至原来的三倍，钢轨最长可用十年才需更换。铁轨断裂问题还推动了
钢材测试设备的研制和测试标准的制定，进一步提高了耐久性。
en: The building of rail lines, which accounted for the largest use of steel in this period, illustrates the effects of this durability. During the early years of steam railway travel, before the 1860s, rails were made of wrought iron, which carried heavier traffic than the perishable wooden tracks used by horse-drawn railways but was liable to fracture under repeated loads and needed replacing every six to twelve months, and later every thirty-six months. Fractured rails were a frequent cause of train accidents, and their inspection and replacement were a major cost. With the switch to steel after the 1860s, the replacement period increased threefold, the rails lasting as long as a decade before replacement was required. The problem of rail breaks also spurred the
development of machines and standards for testing steels, which further improved durability.

zh: 技术形式与合成材料的持久性，使不同时间段之间形成一种不同关系：当下的新计划推动者可以设计安排，以大规模、新颖的方式从未来的生活中获利。这些安排虽非全新，却代表人类致富与致贫方式的显著扩张。多数关于资本主义现代性的叙述未能理解这一变化。
en: The persistence of technical forms and synthetic materials made possible a different relationship between periods of time, one in which the promoters of new schemes in the present could develop arrangements to profit in large and novel ways from lives in the future. These arrangements, while not entirely new, represented a significant expansion of modes of human enrichment and impoverishment. It is a change that most accounts of capitalist modernity fail to understand.

zh: 一种向未来征税的装置
en: A Device for Taxing the Future

zh: 解释技术圈转变如何改变经济生活组织的常规方式，从“需求”增长开始。据说，大型结构和技术系统提供了满足不断扩张的人类
的机会：更快的旅行、远距离通信、更多材料运输、建造更高更大的城市，以及殖民和耕作未开发或开发较少的土地。这些需求又解释了 1860 年代后政治经济组织的深刻变化。据说，宏大的工程和交通项目需要扩大的管理控制来应对其复杂性，也需要大量资本。这些要求催生了一种新装置，它将在此后一个半世纪中成为强大的政治力量：由投资者所有的大型商业公司。
en: The conventional way to explain how transformations of the technosphere altered the organisation of economic life starts from an increase in ‘demand’. Large structures and technical systems provided the opportunities, it is said, to meet expanding human

: for faster travel, communication over greater distances, the increased transportation of materials, the building of taller and larger cities, and the colonising and farming of undeveloped or less intensively exploited lands. These demands, in turn, provide the explanation for a profound change in political-economic organisation in the period after the 1860s. Grand engineering and transportation projects required an expanded managerial control to handle their complexity, we are told, and great quantities of capital. Those requirements brought forth a novel apparatus, one that was to become a powerful political force over the following century and a half: the large, investor-owned business corporation.

zh: 技术圈的扩张以及大企业的兴起，通常由这类计划的推动者从有待满足的需求来解释。他们许诺，铁路、船用运河、能源基础设施、土地开发和其他项目将运送大量新的人员、粮食和制成品。然而事实上，其中许多项目——北美的横贯大陆铁路，甚至初开时的苏伊士运河——常常难以找到使用者，难以收回成本。它们通常超出预算，且往往损害人类社区和更广泛的生命系统。这些项目事实上往往是为另一个目的建造的：主要不是为了运送人和货物，而是——正如一项对美国横贯大陆铁路的研究所示——为了运送纸张。
让我们更仔细地考察基础设施如何运送纸张——如何成为
制造债务的工具，创造出的不是运载人与货物的载具，而是制造非劳动收入的工具。
en: Expansion of the technosphere – and the rise of large business – was typically explained by the promoters of such schemes in terms of demands to be met. They promised that railways, ship canals, energy infrastructure, land development, and other projects would allow the movement of great new quantities of people, food supplies, and manufactured goods. In fact, however, many of them – the transcontinental railways of North America, even the Suez Canal when first opened – often struggled to find users and pay their way. They were typically over budget and often detrimental to human communities and to wider systems of life. The projects were in fact often built for a different purpose: not primarily to move people and goods, but, as a study of the American transcontinental railways shows us, to move paper.
Let us consider more closely how infrastructure moves paper – by becoming
the instrument for the manufacture of debt, creating vehicles not for the movement of people and goods, but for the making of unearned income.

zh: 长距离钢制铁路、密集建设和电气化的城市、重新工程化的河流系统，以及其他大型耐久安排，其意义并不主要在于产生了为支付建设费用而筹集资本的需要。诚然，支付建设费用的资金必须筹措，通常是借助进一步的信用货币体系：例如美国铁路建设不是用储蓄融资，而是通过银行创造的债务，包括以授予的土地作抵押，由未来的土地使用者偿还；在欧洲，建设铁路、矿山和其他碳密集基础设施的人，常常用“供应商股份”支付承包商和供应商，给予他们对预期利润的索取权；在埃及，正如我们将看到的，政府通过允许阿斯旺大坝的主要推动者发行一种新货币来支付大坝建设费用，其价值基于未来的税收收入。
这些项目的耐久性和规模，并未要求大量从过去积累的资金，反而创造了来自未来的可靠而丰沛的收入流，形式包括客运票价、货运费、航运通行费、城市租金收入、抵押贷款支付，以及对农业用地增加的地租和税收。拥有适当政治和法律保障的项目推动者，可以在当下出售这些预期收入的股份。在当下出售未来收入索取权的机会，随着蒸汽动力交通和燃煤电力的发展而迅速扩大，代表的不是对资本的
，而是碳密集地
资本的手段。我们关于资本的一切传统观念——那个被想象为从过去积累起来的基金的托词——一旦开始研究资本如何被创造，就会崩塌。
en: The long-distance, steel-formed railway, the densely built and electrified city, the re-engineered river system, and other large, durable arrangements created not so much a need to raise capital to pay for them, although such payments had to be found, typically through further systems of credit money: the building of US railways, for example, was financed not from savings but through debt created by banks, including via mortgages on land grants, to be repaid by future users of the land; in Europe, those building railways, mines, and other carbonintensive infrastructure often paid their contractors and suppliers in ‘vendor shares’, giving them a claim on prospective profits; and in Egypt, as we will see, the government paid for the Aswan Dam by allowing its chief promoter to issue a new kind of money, whose value was based on future tax receipts.

Rather than requiring significant funds accumulated from the past, the durability and scale of such projects created a reliable and plentiful stream of revenue from the future, in the form of passenger fares, freight charges, shipping tolls, urban rental incomes, mortgage payments, and increased rents and taxes on agricultural land. The promoter of the project, armed with the proper political and legal guarantees, could offer to sell shares in that prospective income in the present. The opportunity to sell future claims to income in the present, expanding rapidly with the development of steam-powered transportation and coal-fired electric power, represented not a
for capital, but a means for its carbon-heavy
. All our conventional ideas about capital, that alibi imagined as a fund accumulated from the past, collapse once we start to study how capital is created.

zh: 十九世纪末，股份公司、商业银行和土地开发公司的数量突然激增——不仅在欧洲和北美，也在开罗、伊斯坦布尔以及北大西洋世界之外的其他地区——代表着一种不断扩张的资本化方法。技术圈的改造已成为一种系统，不仅用于人类对共同世界的殖民，也用于支配来自共同未来的收入。资本的创造，以及资本与劳动的关系，一直作为对未来的索取权运作；如今由于有更多可能性建造更耐久的装置，在当下生成并控制从未来获得的收入流，这种关系得以呈现为一种延展的时间结构。
en: The sudden explosion in the number of joint-stock firms, commercial banks, and land development companies in the late nineteenth century, in Europe and North America but also in places like Cairo and Istanbul and other areas outside the North Atlantic world, represented an expanding method of capitalisation. The modification of the technosphere had become a system not just for the human colonisation of the common world, but for the command of revenue from the common future. The creation of capital, and the relation between capital and labour, which had always operated as claims upon the future, could take on an extended temporal structure, thanks to the wider possibilities now available to build more durable apparatuses for generating and controlling in the present a stream of revenue obtained from the future.

zh: 借用德勒兹与加塔利的术语，我们可以把股份公司视为一种作为“攫取装置”运作的装配体。

这一说法提请注意未来攫取所依赖的物质、权力、辩护、测量、计算和强制等多种形式。这套装置既非完全公共，也非完全私人，而是兼有两者；既由物质构成，也由观念构成；既部署法律，也部署暴力；既依赖精细计算，也依赖对预期世界的想象性建构。金融家和铁路经济学家——尤其在美国——发展了计算工具，以及关于铁路里程、煤炭消耗、客运和货运量的统计数据，用来估算预期收入并计算其现值。推动者通过报纸和广告宣传活动宣传和吹嘘一项计划，发现他们能以数倍于建造装置成本的价格出售股份。他们出售的不再只是当下的资产和设备安排。由于拥有对未来收入的索取权，这套装置已成为一台攫取和转移未来收入的技术—法律—政治机器。
en: Adopting a term from Deleuze and Guattari, we can think of the joint-stock company as an assemblage that operates as an ‘apparatus of capture’.

The phrase draws attention to the multiple forms of material, power, justification, measurement, calculation, and coercion on which a capture of the future depends. The apparatus is neither fully public nor private but combines aspects of both; is made up of both materials and ideas; deploys both law and violence; and depends upon both careful calculation and the imaginative construction of prospective worlds. Financiers and railroad economists, especially in the United States, developed the tools of calculation, and the statistical data on miles of track, consumption of coal, and volumes of passengers and freight carried, that were used to estimate the prospective income, and calculate its present value. Publicising and puffing a venture through newspapers and advertising campaigns, promoters discovered they could sell shares at many times the cost of building the apparatus. They were no longer selling just a present arrangement of assets and equipment. Thanks to its claim on later revenues, the apparatus had become a machine – technical, legal, and political – for the capture and transfer of future income.

zh: 向股东支付股息，变成企业带入未来的一项收费。这项收费如今是经营成本，在计算——以铁路为例——未来客运和货运费率、未来雇员工资和福利时必须考虑。承担这些成本，成为伟大的德国社会经济学家马克斯·韦伯所诊断的对未来使用者的一种征税。在 1894 年发表的关于汉堡和柏林证券交易所及其他欧洲金融市场的详细调查中，他描述了工人和乘客，以及通过铁路运输货物的购买者，如何因抽取这些当代形式的“贡赋”而被“征税”。
作为一种组织对这种收入之索取权的装置，股份公司是一台从未来获取贡赋的机器，把预期收入从一般民众手中转移到当下的企业家和投资者手中。
en: The payment of a dividend to share owners became a charge carried by the enterprise into the future. The charge was now a cost of doing business, to be considered in calculating – in the case of railways, for example – future rates for transporting passengers and freight and future wages and benefits of employees. The carrying of those costs became what the great German social economist Max Weber diagnosed as a tax on future users. In a detailed investigation of the Hamburg and Berlin stock exchanges and other European financial markets, published in 1894, he described how both workers and passengers, as well as the purchasers of goods shipped via rail, were now ‘taxed’ by the extraction of these contemporary forms of ‘tribute-duties’.

As an apparatus that organised claims to this revenue, the joint-stock company operated as a machine for obtaining tribute from the future, moving prospective income from the general population into the hands of entrepreneurs and investors in the present.

zh: 时间机器
en: Time Machines

zh: 投资者所有的公司在此前已有其他形式，但它们随着新的燃煤基础设施项目和随之扩张的殖民活动而大量出现，情况
有所不同。从十六世纪到十八世纪，欧洲建立了许多大型股份公司，通常通过立法或皇家特许状，作为国家赞助的贸易和殖民工具。
与更早的商人冒险家公司或欧洲城市同盟相比——后者为其商人成员在波罗的海和黎凡特等邻近地区建立贸易垄断——或与更古老的商人合伙形式相比，后者曾数百年管理横跨印度—伊斯兰世界的贸易，欧洲特许股份公司建造了一套异常机动、致命的攫取装置，可以在远距离上控制。
它们采用阿拉伯航海者的多功能三角帆，以及阿拉伯船舶设计和导航仪器，并将其与武器、纪律和复兴的十字军意识形态结合起来，建造跨洋武装商船，以及船只可以避难、贸易和整修的设防海外港口。
在煤炭和钢铁时代之前，远洋船舶是常规生产中最大、最昂贵的技术装置，而暴力、垄断性的殖民贸易则是从未来获利的主要领域：通过出售武装航行的股份、贴现汇票和出售保险合同。跨大西洋贩运非洲奴隶，以及从加勒比种植园（奴隶被强迫在那里劳动）运出糖，为资本化未来收入创造了更多、更长期的机会。
en: Investor-owned companies had existed in earlier forms, but their proliferation in association with new coal-driven infrastructure projects and the expanding colonisation that accompanied them was something

rather different. From the sixteenth to the eighteenth centuries, numerous large joint-stock companies were established in Europe, usually by legislative or royal charter, as an instrument of state-sponsored trade and colonisation.

Compared with earlier companies of merchant adventurers or leagues of European cities, which established for their merchant membership trading monopolies in adjacent regions like the Baltic and the Levant, or the even older forms of merchant partnership that had managed trade across the Indo-Islamic world for centuries, the chartered European joint-stock companies built an unusually mobile and lethal apparatus of capture, controllable over long distances.

Adopting the versatile lateen sail from Arab seafarers, along with Arab ship design and navigation instruments, and combining them with weaponry, discipline, and a revived Crusader ideology, they built transoceanic armed trading vessels, along with the fortified overseas harbours where ships could take refuge, trade, and refit.

Before the age of coal and steel, ocean-going ships were the largest and most costly technical devices in regular production, while violent, monopolistic colonial trade was a principal field of profiting from the future, through offering shares in armed voyages, discounting bills of exchange, and selling insurance contracts. The shipping of enslaved Africans across the Atlantic and of sugar from the Caribbean plantations in which they were put to work created additional and longer-term opportunities for capitalising future revenues.

zh: 这些较早形式的股份公司并未延续下去。

它们的强制性和垄断性事业往往代价高昂、不稳定。它们的扩张导致特许它们的欧洲国家之间，以及它们与奥斯曼帝国、莫卧儿帝国和欧洲之外其他强国之间频繁战争。从贸易中获利的机会——同一商品在不同地点之间的价格差——受陆路竞争的制约，也受欧洲缺乏足够有价值、可作为交换而运往海外的商品的限制。公司股份把未来贸易利润的索取权转化为可交易资产，最初只由少数大商人持有，他们主要在公司会议上彼此交易。直到十八世纪之交，更广泛的股份市场才发展起来，危机随即接踵而至。
殖民公司靠未来收入承诺出售股份的能力，导致激烈的竞争和惊人的金融崩溃，最著名的是 1720 年英国南海公司和法国密西西比公司同时崩溃。到
十八世纪末，尽管数量激增，许多殖民股份事业已经失败，或被改造成更强大的东西：帝国属地的政府，如印度、荷属东印度、南部非洲和西印度群岛；或独立的移民殖民联邦，如美国。与此同时，大多数欧洲国内企业仍以家族企业或合伙企业形式经营。股份公司在新基础设施周围的短暂投机热潮中重新出现，例如收费公路、内河航运运河、铜矿和煤矿以及早期铁路的建设。这些股份事业往往股权集中、寿命短暂。
en: These earlier forms of joint-stock company did not endure.

Their coercive and monopolistic ventures tended to be costly and unstable. Their expansion led to frequent warfare among the European states that chartered them and with the Ottoman and Mughal Empires and other powers outside Europe. The opportunities to profit from trade – from the difference in price of the same good in one location and another – were limited by competition from overland routes and the lack of European goods that were valuable enough to be shipped in return. The shares in the companies, through which the claims on future profits from trade were converted into tradeable assets, were held initially among a limited group of large merchants, who traded the stock mostly among themselves at company meetings. Only at the turn of the eighteenth century did a wider market in shares develop, and crises soon followed.

The ability of colonising companies to sell shares on the promise of future revenue led to intensive rivalries and spectacular financial crashes, most famously the collapse in 1720 of both the South Sea Company in England and the Mississippi Company in France. By

the end of the eighteenth century, even as their numbers proliferated, many of the colonising joint-stock ventures had failed, or were being re-engineered as something stronger: the governments of imperial dependencies, as in India, the Dutch East Indies, southern Africa, and the islands of the West Indies; or independent settler-colonial federations such as the United States. Meanwhile, most domestic European businesses continued to operate as family-owned firms or partnerships. Joint-stock companies reappeared in brief frenzies of speculation around a new infrastructure, such as the building of toll roads, inland shipping canals, copper and coal mines, and the early railways. These joint-stock ventures tended to be closely held and short-lived.

zh: 现代商业公司并非从这些较早形式自然演化而来。它出人意料地出现在十九世纪后期，最初有一个主要目的：从修建大型铁路中获利。伦敦、巴黎、汉堡和纽约证券交易所交易的大多数股份属于铁路公司，以及与铁路建设相关的企业和投资银行。
电报公司、轮船公司、电力和照明公司以及钢铁公司也交易未来利润的股份。大型企业——这个将主导二十世纪政治的政治—法律装置——起源于以碳燃料为动力、以钢铁建造、支配地形的基础设施所开创的未来抽取新模式。
en: The modern business corporation did not evolve naturally from such earlier forms. It emerged unexpectedly, in the later nineteenth century, initially for one main purpose: to profit from building large railways. The great majority of shares traded on the stock exchanges of London, Paris, Hamburg, and New York were in railway companies, along with businesses and investment banks associated with railway construction.

Telegraph firms, steamship lines, electric power and light companies, and iron and steel companies also traded shares in future profits. The large business firm, the politico-legal apparatus that would dominate the politics of the twentieth century, had its origins in the novel mode of extraction from the future inaugurated by carbon-fuelled, steel-built, terrain-commanding infrastructure.

zh: 这些企业的独特之处，与其说在于规模或复杂性，不如说在于它们在时间中的持续方式，使它们能够在较长时期内攫取预期收入。这种长寿部分来自用钢铁和混凝土等被赋予新用途的材料建造基础设施，这些材料可望服务数年或数十年。然而，耐久性也来自新的政治力量形式。交通线路和能源网络的规模与延伸，以及城市开发、灌溉项目和其他宏大工程，不仅依赖材料耐久性，也依赖法律、权威、强制和辩护的耐久安排。新装配体的韧性不仅是技术问题，也是技术政治问题。
en: What distinguished these businesses was not so much their size or complexity but their mode of persistence in time, allowing the capture of prospective revenue over extended periods. The longevity arose in part, as mentioned, from the creation of infrastructure from repurposed materials, such as steel and concrete, which promised years or decades of service. However, the durability also arose from new forms of political strength. The scale and extension of transportation lines and energy networks, along with urban development, irrigation projects, and other immense schemes, depended not just on material durability but upon durable arrangements of law, authority, compulsion, and justification. The resilience of new assemblages was a question not merely of technics but of technopolitics.

zh: 伴随股份公司兴起的政治转型有几个组成部分。首先是新法律形式的发展。法律上的两项变化常被提及：设立股份公司须经立法机构法案的要求逐渐取消，以及 1860 年代前后“有限责任原则的
非凡扩张”。
然而，另外两项法律创新更重要，却常被忽视。第一，股份本身成为一种财产形式。此前，购买公司股票意味着取得一份股份，代表对某一船舶及其货物，或铁路公司的车场、棚屋、机车车辆和线路的部分所有权。股份本身不是法律上的一项财产，而是一种记录对这项物质资产之索取权的方式。到十九世纪后期，股份已变成一种自身独立的、全新类型的财产。它成为拥有公司未来收益一部分的手段，其价值与企业的物质资产没有直接关系。
保护它的警务、政治权力、帝国威胁、金融计算、保险和经济辩护形式越强，未来收入的承诺就越大，股份也就越有价值。
en: The political transformations accompanying the rise of joint-stock companies had several components. There was the development of novel legal forms. Two changes in law are often noted: the gradual removal of the requirement for an act of the legislature to establish a joint-stock company and, around the 1860s, the ‘extraordinary
expansion of the principle of Limited Liability’.

Two other legal innovations, however, were more significant but are often overlooked. First, the share itself became a form of property. Previously, to purchase stock in a company had been to acquire a share that represented the part ownership of, say, a vessel and its cargo or a railway company’s yards, sheds, rolling stock, and lines. The share was not itself a piece of property in law, but, rather, a way of recording a claim on this material asset. By the later nineteenth century, the share had changed into a form of property in its own right and of a new kind. It had become a means of owning part of the company’s future earnings, its value bearing no direct relation to the material assets of the business.

The stronger the forms of policing, political power, imperial threat, financial calculation, insurance, and economic justification that protected it, the greater the promise of future revenue and thus the more valuable the share.

zh: 第二，值得注意的是，这种根本性的新财产形式被永久化了。其他通过类似法律手段建立的“纸面”财产权，例如发明专利权或文学艺术作品的版权，都有期限，只持续固定年数。十九世纪中叶以前，股份公司及其股份也是如此。在多数情况下，注册为公众公司的权利是一种会到期的安排。公司特许状有期限，通常二十或三十年，银行更短。英格兰银行是一家股份公司，其特许状每十一年到期一次。
其他特许状在股东收回初始投资后到期。例如在马萨诸塞州，1805 年《收费公路公司法》允许立法机构在从道路使用者收取的通行费收入达到建造成本加 12% 后解散公司，此后收费公路转为公共所有。
到十九世纪后期，股份获得了永久存续的可能性。
尽管它仍面临贬值甚至因公司崩溃而失效的风险，但作为对未来收益或回报的索取权，它已不再类似于租约、版权、专利或其他有期限的索取权，而类似于永久的财产所有权，在这一点上类似于土地或其他不动产的完全保有产权。
en: Second, remarkably, this fundamentally new form of property was made perpetual. Other ‘paper’ property rights established through analogous legal means, such as the patent on an invention or the copyright on a literary or artistic work, were limited in duration, lasting a fixed number of years. Before the mid-nineteenth century, the same was true of a joint-stock company and its shares. The right to incorporate as a public company was, in most cases, an arrangement that expired. Corporate charters were awarded for a limited period, typically twenty or thirty years, with a shorter limit in the case of banks. The charter of the Bank of England, a joint-stock company, expired every eleven years.

Other charters expired once the shareholders had recouped their initial investment. In Massachusetts, for example, the Turnpike Corporation Act of 1805 allowed the legislature to dissolve the corporation when earnings from the tolls on road users reached the cost of construction plus 12 per cent, after which the turnpike became public.
By the late nineteenth century, the share had acquired the possibility of perpetual life.

While it carried the risk of losing value or even, with the collapse of a company, expiring, as a right to future earnings or yields it became analogous not to a lease, copyright, patent, or other time-delimited claim, but to a perpetual right of ownership, similar in this way to the freehold of land or other real property.

zh: 不断扩张的未来攫取装置帮助产生了另一种新财产形式：风险的所有权。资本化过程的传播创造了衡量风险、管理风险生产并从中获利的新方式——用我们后文将探讨的术语说，就是风险的“经济化”。
正如

我们将在下一章看到的，对尼罗河的毁灭将通过以新方式生产洪水“风险”并资本化这一威胁来获得辩护。因债务而丧失土地或住房（止赎）的危险，在同一时期广泛出现于埃及和世界各地，为组织物质强制和道德义务提供了新手段。但正如本书将贯穿探讨的，风险同样是从未来获利的新方法之源。这一时期铁路和其他大型工程的建设，助推了事故保险公司的发展；这些公司可以为个人事故风险赋值，并将其转化为可交易资产。保险公司此前只在为远洋帆船及其货物承保的专门领域运作，如今成长为这种新金融资产的大规模交易者。
芝加哥（谷物）和开罗（棉花）等城市的商品期货市场，依赖电报、谷物提升设备和其他技术机制的发展，产生了另一种可交易资产：把风险——此处是价格波动风险——与它所依附的对象分离。
en: The expanding apparatuses for the capture of the future helped produce another novel form of property: the ownership of risk. The spread of capitalisation processes was creating new ways of measuring risk, managing its production, and profiting from (to use a term we will explore later) its ‘economisation’.
The destruction of the River Nile, as

we will see in the next chapter, was to be justified by the production in new ways of the ‘risk’ of its flooding and the capitalisation of that threat. The danger of losing one’s land or one’s housing in foreclosure for debt, emerging widely in the same period in Egypt and across the world, provided a novel means of organising material compulsion and moral obligation. But, as we will explore throughout this book, risk was equally the source of new methods of profiting from the future. The building of railways and other large ventures in this period helped trigger the development of accident insurance corporations, which could assign a value to the risk of personal accident and transform it into a tradeable asset. Previously working only in the specialised sphere of insuring longdistance sailing vessels and their cargoes, insurance companies now grew into large-scale traders of this new financial asset.

The development of commodity futures markets in cities such as Chicago (for grain) and Cairo (for cotton), dependent on the development of the telegraph, the grain elevator, and other technical mechanisms, generated another tradeable asset derived from separating the risk, in this case of price fluctuations, from the object to which it was attached.

zh: 伴随这些法律和技术变化的，是强制力量的发展。警察力量、动员的民兵和军队作为铁路线和其他基础设施的使用者和保护者扩大权力，而基础设施的安全越来越成为部署他们的理由。
帝国战争和殖民占领可以被合理化为保障新交通通道的需要，例如苏伊士运河，或这些路线所依赖的加煤站以及后来的石油设施；或者为了殖民一条被重新工程化为灌溉系统的河流上游，例如英国在 1890 年代为其入侵苏丹提出的论点。
en: Accompanying these legal and technical changes was the development of coercive power. Police forces, mobilised militiamen, and troops extended their powers as both users and protectors of rail lines and other infrastructure, whose security was an increasing justification for their deployment.

Imperial warfare and colonial occupation could be rationalised by the need to secure new communication routes, such as the Suez Canal, or the coaling stations and later the oil installations on which those routes depended, or to colonise the upper reaches of a river re-engineered as an irrigation system, as with the British argument in the 1890s for its invasion of Sudan.

zh: 大型技术装配体的时代也是“帝国的时代”：在这个时期，少数欧洲强国以及美国和日本，开始把较旧的军事和商业支配模式，转变为对欧洲和美洲以外大部分地区的正式兼并和政治控制。
技术圈扩张与帝国权力扩张之间有何联系？我们必须再次谨慎对待解释的方向。人们容易假定，帝国国家总是支持更大型的交通、通信和控制基础设施。但这一解释很少经得起仔细检验，苏伊士运河和巴拿马运河、连接维也纳与伊斯坦布尔的横贯奥斯曼铁路、英国统治下的
印度铁路，或北美横贯大陆铁路等项目都表明了这一点。
尽管推动者通常声称这些项目服务于西方商业和帝国的需要，但帝国贸易或通信创造需求的情况很少见。相反的情况可能更接近实际：建造超大型结构以攫取未来支付的机会，往往具有殖民性质。对地方和人民的支配，以及对未来的政治攫取，作为帝国工程更容易组织和辩护。
en: The age of large technical assemblages was also the ‘age of empire’, the period in which a handful of European powers, along with the United States and Japan, began transforming older modes of military and commercial domination into the formal annexation and political control of most areas outside Europe and the Americas.

What was the connection between an expanding technosphere and expanding imperial power? Again, we must be careful about the direction of the explanation. It is easy to assume that imperial states always favoured larger infrastructures of transportation, communication, and control. But that explanation for the rapid expansion of the technosphere seldom survives close inspection, as shown by such projects as the Suez and Panama Canals, the trans-Ottoman railway connecting Vienna to Istanbul, the
Indian railways under British rule, or the transcontinental North American railways.

Although their promoters usually claimed that these projects were serving the needs of Western commerce and empire, it was seldom the case that imperial trade or communication created the demand for them. The reverse may be closer to what happened: the opportunity to build exceptionally large structures for the capture of payments from the future tended to be colonising in form. The command over places and people, and the political capture of the future, were more easily organised and justified as an imperial project.

zh: 脆弱性
en: Vulnerability

zh: 如果这些技术、法律和政治安排形式都促成了资本化新模式的耐久性和规模，那么它们的范围和持续时间也成了脆弱性的来源。它们引入了非凡的不稳定——这些不稳定定义了当前的集体困境。
en: If these forms of technical, legal, and political arrangement all contributed to the durability and scale of the new modes of capitalisation, their scope and duration was also the source of vulnerability. They introduced extraordinary instabilities – instabilities that define our current collective predicament.

zh: 第一，通过发展铁路、河流网络、运河、城市扩张和其他计划来攫取未来，造成了地球系统的大规模改变，引发反复的生态危机，摧毁整个人类和非人类生命形式。我们已经注意到，尼罗河的重新工程化如何导致整个国家生态平衡所依赖的洪水脉冲消失；下一章将详细探讨这场毁灭。印度东部的孟加拉和奥里萨三角洲、次大陆西北部的印度河流域，以及欧洲人扩展殖民统治之处的其他大河，都遭受了类似破坏。
铁路也能带来同样严重的扰乱，既有直接的景观改变，也有间接的破坏：草原和原始森林消失、病原体传播，以及伴随生存经济被摧毁和原住民被更快消灭而来的种族灭绝和大规模屠杀，尤其是在美洲。
en: First, the capture of the future through the development of railways, river networks, canals, urban expansion, and other schemes caused the modification of Earth systems on a scale that caused repeated ecological crises, undermining entire forms of human and nonhuman life. We have already noted how the re-engineering of the River Nile led to the elimination of the flood pulse on which the ecological balance of an entire country had depended, a destruction to be explored in detail in the next chapter. Similar damage was caused to the Bengal and Orissa deltas in eastern India, to the Indus Basin in the northwest of the subcontinent, and to other great rivers wherever Europeans extended their colonial rule.

Railways could bring equally significant disruption, both directly, through the modification of the landscape, and indirectly, through the destruction of grasslands and old-growth forests, the spread of pathogens, and the forms of genocide and mass killing that accompanied the elimination of subsistence and the more rapid extermination of native peoples, especially in the Americas.

zh: 第二，从长期看，新尺度的大地破坏还带来另一个破坏稳定的后果，其严重程度不亚于栖息地、物种和人口的毁灭。既然耐久结构和合成材料需要让材料抵抗与其他元素的互动，从而抵抗普通腐烂，它们的建造或合成通常需要大量工艺热。
通过迫使化学键断裂和重组，高温可以硬化、分裂、提纯或化合元素，例如在窑中加热石灰石制造水泥，在熔炉中加热铁矿石生产铁和钢，在反应器中加热大气氮制造肥料和弹药，或在炼油厂加热原油制造燃料和石化产品。使用新耐久基础设施的承运者和运输工具——铁路交通和远洋航运，以及此后的机械化公路运输——也依赖燃烧热。加热产生了废料。与地球系统的其他部分不同，这些废料大多没有成为其他过程的原料，因而没有被循环利用。
en: Second, in the longer term, there was another destabilising consequence to the new scale of breaking of the earth, as serious as the destruction of habitats, species, and human populations. Since durable structures and synthetics required making materials resistant to interaction with other elements and thus to ordinary decay, their construction or synthesis typically required the use of great quantities of process heat.

By forcing chemical bonds to break down and re-form, high temperatures could harden, split, purify, or combine elements, as with the heating of limestone in a kiln to make cement, iron ore in a smelter to produce iron and steel, atmospheric nitrogen in a reactor to create fertiliser and munitions, or crude oil in a refinery to manufacture fuels and petrochemicals. The carriers and haulers that used the new durable infrastructures – rail traffic and ocean shipping, followed by mechanised road transport – also depended on combustion heat. The heating created waste products. Unlike other parts of the Earth system, most of this waste did not become the feedstock for other processes and thus was not recycled.

zh: 燃烧的主要废料是一种气体——二氧化碳，它简单地在空气中累积，数量逐渐超过其他生物与非生物要素将其重新纳入循环的能力。不到一个世纪后，到 1960 年代，使用红外气体分析仪的测量已经表明，这种累积正在改变大气中的气体平衡。二十年后，人们越来越清楚，由此产生的温室效应正在以数千年未见的速率使地球表面变暖。到二十世纪末，人们已普遍理解，这种未被重新纳入循环的废料的生产和累积将终结相对稳定、自我调节的生命过程平衡——自 12,000 年前末次冰期结束以来，这种平衡一直支撑着人类和非人类生命繁荣的条件。
en: The principal waste product of combustion was a gas, carbon dioxide, which simply accumulated in the air, in quantities that gradually exceeded the ability of other living and non-living elements to recycle it. Within less than a century, by the 1960s, measurements using an infrared gas analyser were able to show that this accumulation was changing the balance of gases in the atmosphere. Two decades later, it was increasingly clear that the resulting greenhouse effect was warming the surface of the Earth at a rate not seen in millennia. By the end of the twentieth century, it was widely understood that this production and accumulation of unrecycled waste would bring to a close the relatively stable, self-regulating balance of life processes that, since the ending of the last glacial period 12,000 years ago, had supported the conditions for the flourishing of human and nonhuman life.

zh: 第三，1860 年代后技术圈的大扩张产生了另一股破坏稳定的力量，当时的作家为此引入了一个新术语。他们称之为“资本主义”。
en: Third, the great expansion of the technosphere after the 1860s gave rise to a further destabilising force, for which writers of the period introduced a new term. They called it ‘capitalism’.

zh: 在后来的几十年里，资本主义一词被用于更广泛的意义，追溯更长的历史发展，其起源在于制造业中劳动的重组，甚至更早的商业变化。
那些先前事件很重要，我们将在
进一步探讨。但“资本主义”一词最初是在十九世纪后期使用的，用来描述一个更具体的过程；这个过程在当时的突然扩张，在英国的主要经济思想家阿尔弗雷德·马歇尔和 J. A. 霍布森，以及当时被引用最多的美国经济学家戴维·埃姆斯·韦尔斯看来，比包括第一波工业化在内的更早变化更为重要。
这个新术语指资本家的扩张活动；当时所谓资本家，指金融家或投机者，
即组织信用创造并从信用货币流动中获利的人。
en: In later decades, the word capitalism was used in a more general sense, to trace a longer historical development, with its origins in the reorganisation of labour in manufacturing, if not earlier commercial changes.
Those previous events were significant; we will explore them further in

. But the expression ‘capitalism’ was first used in the late nineteenth century to characterise a more specific process, one whose sudden expansion in that period appeared to leading economic thinkers like Alfred Marshall and J. A. Hobson in England and David Ames Wells, the most cited American economist of the period, to be a more significant change than earlier mutations, including the first wave of industrialisation.
The new term referred to the expanding activities of the capitalist, meaning, at that time, the financier or speculator, the
person who organised the creation of credit and profited from the flow of credit money.

zh: 尽管向现代资本主义的决定性转变常被定位得更早，在工厂制度和工业化中，但股份公司是占有剩余的一种新的、更有效的装置。如果说工厂是一种技术政治时间机器，部分通过延长工作日并加快其中的劳动节奏运作，同时也——正如我们将看到的——通过“雇佣劳动”这一信用装置运作，那么大型技术结构，连同它们所催生的股份公司和股份银行，则代表另一种机器：它不是通过压缩生产时间或通过工资运作个人信用和债务来从劳动中抽取剩余，而是通过更广泛的方法把未来转移到当下。让我们更仔细地考察这个新人物“资本家”及其在这一破坏稳定的过程中的角色。我们可以从某个具体个人的案例开始；此人后来在一些计划中——包括对尼罗河的毁灭——扮演了关键角色。
en: While the decisive shift to modern capitalism is often located earlier, in the factory system and industrialisation, the joint-stock corporation was a new and more effective device for the appropriation of surplus. If the factory was one kind of technopolitical time machine, operating partly by extending and then speeding up the working day but also – as we will see – through the credit device of ‘wage labour’, then large technical structures, along with the joint-stock companies and joint-stock banks to which they gave rise, represented a different machine, one that extracted surplus from labour not by the compression of production time or the working of individual credit and debt through the wage, but by wider methods for the transfer of the future into the present. Let us look more closely at this new figure, the ‘capitalist’, and his role in this process of destabilisation. We can begin with the case of a particular individual, one who was to have a pivotal part in, among other schemes, the destruction of the River Nile.

zh: 自动装填
en: Self-Loading

zh: 出生于德国的英国银行家欧内斯特·卡塞尔爵士，从埃及殖民中获利超过任何其他资本家。
这些年间耐久性与不稳定性之间的关系，以及殖民与灾难之间的关系，可以在他的职业生涯中看到。他与同时代的罗斯柴尔德家族和巴林家族一起，成为十九世纪末伦敦三大金融家之一。与同侪不同，他并非出身商人银行世家，也没有创建这样的家族，因此他的名字如今大多被遗忘。然而，许多年来，他都被认为是欧洲最强的金融家。
他和合伙人所承担的投资项目不断转移焦点，描绘出大型技术系统形式的变迁——金融公司通过这些系统创造信用并从中获利——以及它们对殖民过程的依赖。
en: Sir Ernest Cassel, a German-born British banker, was to profit more than any other capitalist from the colonisation of Egypt.

The relationship between durability and instability in these years, and thus between the colonial and the catastrophic, can be seen in his career. Alongside his contemporaries the Rothschilds and the Barings, Cassel became one of the three largest London-based financiers of the late nineteenth century. Unlike his peers he did not arise from a merchant banking dynasty, nor did he go on to form one, so his name is now largely forgotten. For many years, however, he was considered the strongest financier in Europe.

The shifting focus of investment projects that he and his partners undertook charts the changing forms of large technical systems through which finance houses created and profited from credit – and their dependence on processes of colonisation.

zh: 与许多同侪相比，卡塞尔结合了两种角色：资本家和企业家。也就是说，他既是信用资本的装配者，安排大型基础设施计划所产生的债务或支付承诺，也是这些计划的装配者，把工程师、企业、银行家、殖民地总督和其他掌握帝国权力的人聚集在一起。
en: More than many of his peers, Cassel combined two roles: capitalist and entrepreneur. That is, he was both an assembler of credit capital, arranging the debts or promises to pay that were enabled by large infrastructure schemes, and an assembler of those schemes, bringing together engineers, business firms, bankers, colonial governors, and others wielding imperial power.

zh: 卡塞尔 1870 年代在巴黎一家投资公司 Bischoffsheim and Goldschmidt 开始职业生涯。该公司向埃及总督赫迪夫·伊斯梅尔提供信贷，包括 1870 年用于在尼罗河沿岸发展甘蔗种植园的一笔大额贷款。比绍夫斯海姆以王室糖业地产作抵押创设了这笔贷款，卡塞尔后来控制了这些地产。卡塞尔与比绍夫斯海姆的女婿莫里斯·德·希尔施一起，帮助挽救东方铁路的融资并监督其建设；这是一个奥斯曼项目，旨在用铁路把伊斯坦布尔连接到欧洲各国首都。希尔施男爵把建成的铁路股份卖给柏林的德意志银行，并用所得款项建立了犹太殖民协会——它一度成为世界上最大的慈善组织。该协会计划让乌克兰、立陶宛和俄罗斯帝国其他地区的犹太人口大规模移民到阿根廷的定居点。这反映出铁路建设对想象和实施殖民同样重要，希尔施把阿根廷计划称为“一桩像修建和运营铁路线那样的生意”。
en: Cassel began his career in the 1870s with an investment firm in Paris, Bischoffsheim and Goldschmidt. The firm supplied credit to Khedive Isma‘il, the viceroy of Egypt, including a large loan in 1870 to develop sugar cane plantations on the Nile. Bischoffsheim created the loan via a mortgage on the royal sugar estates, which Cassel was later to control. With Bischoffsheim’s son-in-law, Maurice de Hirsch, Cassel helped to rescue the financing and oversee the construction of the Oriental Railway, an Ottoman project to connect Istanbul by rail to the capital cities of Europe. Baron Hirsch sold his shares in the completed rail line to Deutsche Bank in Berlin and used the proceeds to establish what became for a while the world’s largest charitable organisation, the Jewish Colonisation Association. The association planned for the mass emigration of the Jewish population of Ukraine, Lithuania, and other parts of the Russian Empire to settlements in Argentina. Reflecting the importance of railway building for both imagining and undertaking colonisation, Hirsch called the Argentina scheme a ‘business like that of constructing and operating a railroad line’.

zh: 在希尔施的指导下，卡塞尔着手对美国濒临倒闭的铁路公司进行财务拯救，与后来成为终生朋友的德裔美国金融界领袖雅各布·希夫合作。
1880 年代，卡塞尔把注意力转向欧洲，通过控制炼钢用铁矿石发了财。他接管了瑞典几家陷入困境的铁路公司，这个国家拥有欧洲最大的铁矿藏之一；在贝塞麦炼钢法经过一项小改动后，使用含磷矿石——多数欧洲铁矿，包括瑞典铁矿，都含有这种有害元素——变得可行，他便把相互竞争的线路连接起来运输矿石。
en: Mentored by Hirsch, Cassel undertook the financial rescue of failing railroad firms in the United States, working with a leading German American financier, Jacob Schiff, who became a lifelong friend.

In the 1880s, Cassel turned his attention to Europe, where he made a fortune through the control of iron ore for steelmaking. He took over the struggling railway companies of Sweden, the country with some of Europe’s largest iron deposits, connecting rival lines to ship the ore, after a minor modification to the new Bessemer process for the mass production of steel made it feasible to use ores containing phosphorous, a deleterious element typical of most European supplies, including those of Sweden.

zh: 1890 年代，他重新转向埃及的机会，那里成为他的主要活动领域。埃及未能偿还 1870 年比绍夫斯海姆贷款和其他债务，使欧洲债权人得以控制政府财政；1882 年英国入侵，镇压了一场由军官领导的人民起义，并确立英国的军事占领，进一步强化了这种控制。卡塞尔安排了修建阿斯旺大坝的融资，同时收购了被赫迪夫的欧洲债权人通过止赎取得的糖业地产。大坝成倍放大了这些地产的预期价值，在这些土地被分割并出售给投资者时带来了可观的利润。他还在阿斯旺附近的康翁波村开发了一处甘蔗种植园，安置农户，使之成为一座公司镇。
他把灌溉工程和甘蔗种植园与第三个要素结合起来，帮助组建了
埃及国民银行——一家私人金融财团，投资于大坝限制尼罗河洪水所带来的新土地开发。国民银行还获得了发行埃及纸币的专有权。随后，卡塞尔与法国和埃及的合伙人一起投资了一家炼糖垄断企业，其资产来自收回的赫迪夫产业。我们将会看到，这家糖业垄断企业在经济思想史上扮演了一个奇特的角色。
en: In the 1890s, he turned back to opportunities in Egypt, which became his main field of activity. Egypt’s default on the 1870 Bischoffsheim loan and other debts had allowed the European creditors to take control of the government’s finances, reinforced in 1882 by the British invasion to put down an army-led popular revolt and establish Britain’s military occupation. Cassel arranged the financing to construct the Aswan Dam, and at the same time acquired the sugar estates that had been foreclosed by the Khedive’s European creditors. The dam multiplied the prospective value of the estates, producing a significant profit when the lands were divided and sold to investors. He also developed a sugar plantation, near Aswan, at the village of Kom Ombo, which was settled with farmers and became a company town.
He combined the irrigation works and sugar plantations with a third element, helping to form the

National Bank of Egypt, a private financial consortium for investment in the new land development made possible by the dam’s restriction of the Nile flood. The National Bank also acquired the exclusive right to issue Egyptian bank notes. With French and Egyptian partners Cassel then invested in a sugar-refining monopoly, built from the repossessed assets of the Khedive. The sugar monopoly, as we will see, was to have a curious role in the history of economic thought.

zh: 这些项目依赖英国和其他帝国国家的力量，反过来又帮助扩展了这种力量。其中许多计划依赖铁路和运河为安置和重新安置人口创造的机会。它们还利用了跨领域、跨技术所产生的协同效应，例如铁路建设与铁矿开采，或河流治理与土地投机，或武器制造与帝国战争融资。事实上，这些项目的资本化依赖于这种相互联系、差异和帝国规模；这些特征使信用创造所依赖的风险打包成为可能。卡塞尔对马克沁机枪——世界上第一种自动装填武器——产生兴趣，资助了它的研发，随后帮助组建了一家武器公司——维克斯父子—马克沁公司——从中获利。
与此同时，他直接向扩张殖民计划的政府提供信贷，包括在摩洛哥的法国人，以及从阿斯旺向南推进、占领苏丹的英国人。正是在那里，马克沁机枪展示了它的新威力：推翻穆罕默德·艾哈迈德·本·阿卜杜拉——即马赫迪，或救赎者——的政府；此人曾击败奥斯曼—埃及早先对苏丹的殖民。
en: These projects relied upon the power of Britain and other imperial states, helping in turn to extend that power. Many of the schemes depended on the opportunities that railways and canals created for settling and resettling populations. They also took advantage of the synergies that arose from crossing between different fields and technologies, such as railway building and iron-ore mining, or river control and land speculation, or arms manufacture and the financing of imperial warfare. In fact, the capitalising of these projects depended on such interconnection, difference, and imperial scale; these features allowed the bundling of risk on which credit creation depended. Cassel took an interest in the Maxim machine gun, the world’s first self-loading weapon, and financed its development, then helped form an arms company, Vickers, Sons and Maxim, to profit from it.

At the same time, he extended credit directly to governments expanding their colonisation projects, including the French in Morocco and the British moving south from Aswan to occupy Sudan. It was there that the Maxim gun demonstrated its new powers, in the overthrow of the government of Muhammad Ahmad bin Abd Allah, the Mahdi or redeemer, who had defeated the earlier Ottoman-Egyptian colonisation of Sudan.

zh: 在金融生涯的末期，即二十世纪第一个十年临近结束时，卡塞尔回到了开启其职业生涯的计划——维也纳至伊斯坦布尔的东方铁路——并着手进行一项更为雄心勃勃的扩张。他试图从奥斯曼政府获得一项特许权，把线路延伸到巴格达；该城位于一个当时被怀疑蕴藏大量石油储量的地区中心。
他与朋友雅各布·希夫经常在埃及过冬；两人支持一项计划，利用铁路项目在伊拉克安置来自俄罗斯帝国的犹太殖民者，并结合灌溉和土地开发计划。负责阿斯旺大坝项目和卡塞尔埃及南部糖业种植园的英国工程师被请到巴格达，帮助制订河流开发计划。
在伊拉克建立犹太农业定居点的计划，是希尔施男爵阿根廷计划的后续，也类似于希夫
在美国西南部支持过的一项殖民计划。伊拉克计划把铁路建设、河流开发和土地定居结合起来，旨在把犹太殖民纳入奥斯曼政治秩序，以此挫败新近成立的犹太复国主义组织的对手计划——在巴勒斯坦，即奥斯曼帝国的另一部分，建立一个按种族隔离的犹太国家（像卡塞尔这样成功的帝国金融家，对反犹主义者的愿景毫无兴趣；反犹主义是欧洲正在兴起的政治运动，它把犹太社群视为一个独特的种族或民族）。
在推行这个短命的伊拉克计划的同时，卡塞尔还组建了一个投资者集团，试图获得奥斯曼世界全部石油储备的垄断权，包括埃及和阿拉伯半岛的储备，但未能成功。1921 年去世前不久，卡塞尔最后的行动之一是设立一笔基金，资助新成立的伦敦政治经济学院的经济学教学，并向约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯提供了 5,000 英镑贷款，把这位年轻经济学家（以及未来经济学的拯救者）从印度卢比和其他外币投机失败中解救出来。
en: At the end of his career in finance, towards the close of the first decade of the twentieth century, Cassel returned to the scheme that began his career, the Vienna-to-Istanbul Oriental Railway, and worked on a more ambitious expansion. He tried to obtain from the Ottoman government a concession to extend the line to Baghdad, at the centre of a region now suspected to contain significant reserves of petroleum.

With his friend Jacob Schiff, with whom he had often wintered in Egypt, he supported a plan to use the railway project to settle colonies of Jews from the Russian Empire in Iraq, in association with irrigation and land development schemes. The British engineer responsible for the Aswan Dam project and for Cassel’s sugar plantations in southern Egypt was brought to Baghdad to help with plans for river development.
The project for Jewish rural settlements in Iraq was a successor to Baron Hirsch’s Argentinian scheme and a similar colonisation plan that Schiff

had supported in the southwestern United States. Combining railway building, river development, and land settlement, the Iraq scheme was designed to integrate Jewish colonisation into an Ottoman political order, as a means to thwart the rival plans of the recently established Zionist Organisation for a racially segregated Jewish state in Palestine, another part of the Ottoman Empire (successful imperial financiers like Cassel had no interest in the vision of the antisemites, a rising political movement in Europe that saw Jewish communities as a distinct race or nation).

In combination with the short-lived Iraq scheme, Cassel also formed an investor group that attempted unsuccessfully to acquire monopoly rights to all of the Ottoman world’s oil reserves, including those of Egypt and the Arabian Peninsula. One of Cassel’s final acts, shortly before his death in 1921, was to endow a fund that supported the teaching of economics at the new London School of Economics and to provide a loan of £5,000 to John Maynard Keynes, rescuing the young economist (and future rescuer of economics) from a failed speculation in the Indian rupee and other foreign currencies.

zh: 让我们走进证券交易所
en: Let Us Go into the Stock Exchange

zh: 当我们回到埃及的历史和尼罗河的毁灭时，我们将再次考察卡塞尔，以及他在为阿斯旺大坝和相关制糖计划融资中所扮演的角色，以便更好地理解这些攫取未来的方法。但首先，让我们思考技术圈这些转变，以及资本化手段之耐久性的另一个方面。交易未来的股份，帮助创造了另一个既具稳定作用又具破坏作用的要素，也是卡塞尔本人在生命末期投资的领域：经济学这门学科。作为一门专业学术领域，经济学大约在 1870 年代出现，与现代股票市场、现代帝国主义和现代“资本家”处于同一时期。这并非巧合。
en: When we return to the history of Egypt and the destruction of the Nile, we will look again at Cassel and his role in financing the Aswan Dam and associated schemes to produce sugar, to better understand these methods of capturing the future. But, first, let us consider another aspect of these transformations in the technosphere and the durability of means of capitalisation. Trading shares in that future helped create another element that was both stabilising and disruptive, the enterprise in which Cassel himself invested at the end of his life: the discipline of economics. As a professional academic field, economics emerged around the 1870s, in the same period as modern stock markets, modern imperialism, and the modern ‘capitalist’. This was no coincidence.

zh: 技术圈的殖民改造与现代经济学的诞生之间，有两个连接点。第一，产生股票市场的技术安排，也为经济学这门科学的出现创造了可能。正如我们所见，股份公司创造了一种新资产——股份，它如今显得独立于赋予其价值的物质结构和过程。股份是一种抽象物，一种真实的抽象物，通过法律实践、定价机制、
对劳工抗议的警务镇压以及殖民权力的施加而制造出来。这种抽象化使股份变成一种具有流动性的东西，一种所谓的“金融”资产——它看似不受产生其价值的未来生活形式约束，可以立即与其他金融工具交易。它有一个价格。经济学是同一抽象过程的产物。这门新学科以对不断变动的价格的分析，取代了对殖民、资本和技术圈的研究，而它特殊的抽象方式正是建立在这种价格分析之上。
en: There are two points of connection between the colonising transformation of the technosphere and the birth of modern economics. First, the technical arrangements that produced the stock market also produced the possibility of the science of economics. The joint-stock company, as we have seen, created a new kind of asset, the share, which now appeared to be separate from the material structures and processes from which it acquired its value. The share was an abstraction, and a real one, manufactured through legal practice, pricing mechanisms, the

policing of labour protest, and the imposition of colonial power. This abstracting made the share into something liquid, a so-called ‘financial’ asset—one that, seemingly unconstrained by the future forms of life that produced its value, could be traded instantly for other financial instruments. It had a price. Economics was a product of the same abstraction. The new discipline substituted for the study of colonisation, capital, and the technosphere the analysis of the constantly moving prices on which it built its particular mode of abstraction.

zh: 第二，经济学试图解释，或提供一种托词，来掩盖一种似乎是新“资本主义”特征的非凡现象：非劳动所得。不断扩张的殖民未来的权力，以某种方式在当下产生了空前的意外之财。这种新奇事物需要某种创新的知识体系来解释，并显得能够解决它。什么样的科学，能够通过转移人们对制造财富和不平等的那些机制的注意，来为特殊的财富和不平等形式辩护？经济学的其他历史方面将在后面的某一章讨论，让我们先考察这门新兴学科如何处理非劳动所得问题，即金融现象，并找到它的托词。
en: Second, economics attempted to explain, or provide an alibi for, an extraordinary phenomenon that seemed characteristic of the new ‘capitalism’: unearned income. The expanding power to colonise the future was somehow generating unprecedented windfalls in the present. This novelty required some innovative system of knowledge to explain and appear to resolve it. What kind of science might serve to justify exceptional forms of wealth and inequality, by finding a way to distract attention from the very mechanisms that created them? While other aspects of the history of economics will be considered in a later chapter, let us examine first how the emerging discipline dealt with the problem of unearned income, or the phenomenon of finance, and found its alibi.

zh: 现代金融理论大约在一个多世纪前的同一时期出现，当时正值信用扩张、意外之财和周期性危机频发的时期——这一时期与当下的事件遥相呼应，不仅包括今天的优步和其他科技公司，也包括 2007—8 年全球经济危机。十九世纪末经历了一波股市繁荣，在二十世纪之交达到顶峰，并在 1907 年华尔街大恐慌中崩盘。与一个世纪后的同行一样，当时的经济学家力图理解这些事件。问题在于解释金钱生钱的惊人能力。证券交易所、商业银行、债券交易商和抵押贷款公司成倍增加，不仅出现在北大西洋世界的金融中心，也出现在布宜诺斯艾利斯、开罗、孟买和圣彼得堡等地。
大金融家赚取（有时也失去）了巨额财富，但即使是小投资者也能购买债券或股票，并且不必自己付出任何努力，就能受益于货币那种奇特的增长能力。
en: The modern theory of finance emerged at the same time, just over a century ago, in a period of credit expansion, windfalls, and periodic crises – a period that echoes the events of the present, including not just the Ubers and other tech firms of today but the global economic crisis of 2007–8. The late nineteenth century experienced a wave of stock market booms, which crested at the turn of the twentieth century and crashed in the great Wall Street Panic of 1907. Like their counterparts a century later, the economists of the day struggled to make sense of these events. The problem was to explain the astonishing power of money to make money. Stock exchanges, commercial banks, bond dealers, and mortgage companies had multiplied, not only in the financial capitals of the North Atlantic world but in places like Buenos Aires, Cairo, Bombay, and St Petersburg.
Large financiers made (and sometimes lost) fortunes, but even small investors could purchase bonds or shares and, with no effort on their own part, benefit from the strange ability of money to grow.

zh: 如何解释货币的这种生殖力？非劳动所得的秘密是什么？对于二十世纪之交的经济学家来说，这个谜题被框定为利息问题——或货币与时间的关系。今天，我们如此习惯于时间流逝使货币增长这一假设，以至于很容易

忘记这个观念的奇特之处。一个世纪前，这或许是经济学的中心谜题。较早解释货币繁殖能力的方式似乎不再合适，甚至不再必要。此前，货币似乎是一种不寻常的、有生命的力量，可以消耗自身却不丧失原有的力量，就像人类劳动或可再生的自然资源。两个世纪前，十九世纪初期的政治经济学家解释说，资本和土地、劳动一样，拥有自己的“生产性作用力”。法国伟大的政治经济学家让-巴蒂斯特·萨伊提供了最有说服力的论述；他 1803 年的《政治经济学概论》建立在亚当·斯密的工作之上，影响力超过了后者。
斯密本人没有系统论述利息，只是把它理解为那些向生产者——财富的真正来源——提供原料和设备的人对劳动产品施加的一种收费。
萨伊提出了一种不同的观点，认为资本本身具有生产性。他写道，当资本被贷出固定期限时，“它的作用力在这段时间内被转移”为一种“物质实体”，例如制造商的“工场、机器、器具、原材料和库存”。在贷款期满时，资本的原始价值“全额返还，并经过生产性使用后仍以完好状态出现”。支付利息类似于使用土地的租金或雇佣劳动的工资。它是资本所有者对货币特殊生产能力之临时使用所收取的租金。
en: What explained this fecundity of money? What was the secret of unearned income? For economists at the turn of the twentieth century, the puzzle was framed as the problem of interest – or the relationship between money and time. Today, we are so accustomed to the assumption that the passage of time allows money to grow that it is easy to

forget the strangeness of this idea. A century ago, it was perhaps the central puzzle of economics. Older ways of explaining money’s powers of reproduction no longer seemed appropriate, or even necessary. Previously, money had appeared to be one of those unusual living forces that can expend itself and yet not lose its original power, like human labour or a renewable natural resource. Two centuries ago, the political economists of the early nineteenth century had explained that capital, like land and labour, possessed its own ‘productive agency’. Jean-Baptiste Say, the great French political economist whose
of 1803 had built upon the work of Adam Smith and surpassed it in influence, offered the most persuasive account.

Smith himself had said nothing systematic about interest, understanding it simply as a charge imposed on the product of labour by those who supplied the producers – the actual source of wealth – with materials and equipment.

Say developed a different view, in which capital itself was productive. When capital is loaned for a fixed period, he wrote, ‘its agency is transferred for that space of time’ into a ‘material substance’ such as the ‘works, machinery, utensils, provisions, and stock in hand’ of a manufacturer. At the end of the loan period, the original value of the capital ‘is returned to the full amount, and emerges in a perfect state from its productive employment’. The payment of interest was similar to the rent paid for the use of land or the wage for the employment of labour. It was the rent charged by the owner of capital for the temporary use of money’s peculiar productive power.

zh: 到十九世纪末，所谓金融资本的大规模扩张使这种解释显得不再合适。一方面，贷款利息的获得与它被用于生产性较高还是较低的用途之间，已没有明确关系。利率已成为由货币市场——证券交易所、债券交易商、商品期货市场以及其他金融工具如今被快速买卖的场所——设定的标准收费。另一方面，这些市场催生了一种新的思想，经济学这门科学，其中产生了对货币生钱能力的另一种解释。
en: By the late nineteenth century, the large expansion of so-called finance capital had made this explanation seem inappropriate. On the one hand, there was no clear relationship between the earning of interest on a loan and whether it was put to a more productive or less productive use. The rate of interest had become a standard charge set by the money markets – stock exchanges, bond traders, commodity futures markets, and other places where financial instruments were now rapidly bought and sold. On the other hand, those markets had given birth to a new kind of thought, the science of economics, from which there emerged a different explanation of the power of money to earn money.

zh: “让我们走进巴黎或伦敦这样大型投资中心的证券交易所，”法国经济学家莱昂·瓦尔拉斯在他 1874 年的著作中写道；该书后来确立了一般均衡理论作为经济学科学的基础。“我们现在将会看到，竞争在一个组织良好的市场中如何运作。”
电报的引入及其价格信息的快速传输，股票行情自动收录机
纸带的出现及其对价格持续变动的视觉展示，股份从物质设备和物理结构的代表转变为抽象的货币工具，以及为每股计算并公布每日收盘价的做法：所有这些物质发展，都使股票市场看起来几乎是买卖双方行动的一个完美模型。
与所有市场一样，“价格”的创造是技术和政治安排的产物。那些控制市场机制的人——电报、股票行情收录机，以及它们所依赖的电线和电池电力——掌控着获取信息的渠道，甚至交易所的会员资格。
但这些物质装置和法律安排产生了一种抽象物，经济理论如今可以围绕它展开。
en: ‘Let us go into the stock exchange of a large investment centre like Paris or London,’ wrote the French economist Léon Walras, in his 1874 text that was to establish general equilibrium theory as the basis of an economic science. ‘We shall see, now, how competition works in a well-organized market.’
The introduction of the telegraph with its rapid transmission of price information, the development of the stock ticker

tape with its visual display of the continuous movement of prices, the transformation of the share from a representation of material equipment and physical structures into an abstract monetary instrument, and the practice of calculating and publishing a daily closing price for each share: all these material developments had made the stock market appear an almost perfect model of buyers and sellers in action.

As with all markets, the creation of a ‘price’ was a product of technical and political arrangements. Those who controlled the market mechanisms – the telegraph, the ticker, and the electrical wiring and battery power on which they depended – managed access to information and even membership in the exchange.
But these material devices and legal arrangements generated an abstraction around which economic theory could now unfold.

zh: 货币市场促成了对财富理解的一次突变。“货币市场这一通常说法并不指任何地点，”与瓦尔拉斯共同创立这门新科学的威廉·杰文斯写道，“它指那些贷出或借入货币、并不断交换商业进程信息的银行家、资本家和其他交易者的总和。”
这个总和，这个看似没有地点的抽象物，使政治经济学得以放弃研究更广阔世界——国家、人口、产业、资源、交通、基础设施、帝国——的尝试，成为一门价格机制的科学。
这种新的思维方式后来被称为“新古典经济学”，它所产生的对资本和利息的理解，在此后一个世纪主导了经济分析。
正如我们将在
看到的，正是这个关于货币的故事，如今似乎无法充分理解我们的困境，尤其是气候危机和所谓经济增长的问题。这种无能可以追溯到以下事实：货币市场——似乎货币可以在其中毫不费力地生钱的地方——不仅提供了有待解释的问题，也提供了新科学从中得出答案的实验室。
en: The money markets facilitated an abrupt change in the understanding of wealth. ‘The common expression Money Market denotes no locality’, wrote William Jevons, a cofounder with Walras of the new science. ‘It is applied to the aggregate of those bankers, capitalists, and other traders who lend or borrow money, and who constantly exchange information concerning the course of business.’

This aggregate, this seemingly placeless abstraction, allowed political economy to abandon its attempts to study the wider world – countries, populations, industries, resources, transportation, infrastructure, empire – and become a science of the price mechanism.
The novel way of thinking, later referred to as ‘neoclassical economics’, produced the understanding of capital and interest that went on to govern economic analysis for the next century.
It is the story of money that today, as we will see in

, seems unable to make adequate sense of our predicament, in particular the problem of climate crisis and so-called economic growth. This inability can be traced to the fact that money markets – the very place where it seemed that money could effortlessly make money – provided not just the problem to be explained, but the laboratory within which the new science produced an answer.

zh: 经济学家试图找到一种替代方案，不再把“生产性作用力”归于资本，而是像新古典经济思想中的其他一切事物一样，把资本何以赚取利息这一问题的答案，主要归于人类偏好的运作。如果人们愿意为现在就拥有货币、而不是在今后某个日期拥有它而支付溢价——换言之，为临时使用资本而支付利息——那么这种意愿必定反映了今天消费而非以后消费的自然倾向。正如美国经济学家欧文·
费雪在《利息率》（1908）中所解释的——这部著作确立了对资本的新理解——货币赚取利息的能力，与技术圈中的转变以及帝国权力的扩张毫无关系，尽管正是后者使以前所未有的规模从未来获取收入成为可能。它只是人类缺乏耐心的结果。
en: Seeking an alternative to attributing a ‘productive agency’ to capital, economists found the solution to the question of how capital could earn interest by attributing this payment, as with everything else in neoclassical economic thought, largely to the operation of a human preference. If people were willing to pay a premium to have money now rather than at a subsequent date – in other words, to pay interest for the temporary use of capital – that willingness must reflect a natural inclination to consume today rather than later. As the American economist Irving
Fisher explained in

(1908), the work that established the new understanding of capital, the power of money to earn interest had nothing to do with the transformations in the technosphere and the expansion of imperial power that had made possible the capture of revenue from the future on an unprecedented scale. It was simply a consequence of human impatience.
body.review: 校注：本章正文记《利息率》为1908年，原注70记为1907年。1908年《Economic Journal》的同期书评明确列出版年份为1907。本章随后“1911年，问世三年后”的说法沿用正文年代；译文均保留底本。 https://academic.oup.com/ej/article-abstract/18/69/66/5291306

zh: 起初，这种从货币的作用力转向人类偏好的变化有其批评者。
资本和利息理论怎能完全不关注生产过程？资本赚取收入的能力，必定与其投入的技术过程有关。对这一反对意见的答案很快找到了，办法是引入另一个人物，以及一个更可靠的托词来源：企业家的形象。
en: At first, this shift from the agency of money to the preferences of humans had its critics.

How could the theory of capital and interest pay no attention to the productive process? Surely the earning power of capital must have something to do with the technical processes into which it was put. An answer to this objection was soon found, by introducing another human agent, and a more reliable source of alibi: the figure of the entrepreneur.

zh: 企业家
en: The Entrepreneur

zh: 在较早的古典经济学家中，也发生过类似的转向。事实上，正是让-巴蒂斯特·萨伊引入了“企业家”一词，来解释财富的生产——以及利息的赚取——如何依赖这一关键人物。萨伊《概论》1803 年的第一版对此谈得很少。但在接下来的十年里，萨伊因拿破仑·波拿巴夺取政权而被迫退出公共生活，便尝试亲自组织一个生产过程。他利用一位富有的姑姨辈亲属和其他投资者的资金，并在弟弟路易的协助下，把法国东北部奥希村上游的一条小河改造成运河，建立了一座水磨坊，把棉纤维纺成纱线。这家企业面临一个反复出现的技术难题：木制机器中把动力从

（水力驱动装置）传送到缠绕纱线的锭子上的部件，不断断裂。用熟铁部件替换木制部件未能消除断裂，再用更坚固但更脆的铸铁部件替换也失败了。与许多想成为工业家的人一样，萨伊发现引入机械化的尝试过于困难。生产中受损材料的浪费——占原棉的 25%——加剧了困难。由于无法从水力机器中获利，萨伊于 1812 年解散了这家企业，成为食利者，投资于若干其他事业。他尤其帮助弟弟接管了一家炼糖企业。炼糖厂比纺织厂更不容易发生故障，因为煮沸和提纯原糖
比把棉纤维纺成细纱的过程更简单。路易·萨伊炼糖公司后来成为法国最成功的制糖企业，也是该国最大的工业企业之一——尽管正如该公司的经理以自己手指的代价所发现的那样，即使在炼糖过程中，工业事故也可能造成后果。
en: Among the earlier, classical economists, a similar move had been made. In fact, it was Jean-Baptiste Say who introduced the term
to explain how the production of wealth – and the earning of interest – depends on this pivotal figure. The first edition of Say’s

, in 1803, said little on the subject. But, over the following decade, forced out of public life by Napoleon Bonaparte’s seizure of power, Say tried his own hand at organising a productive process. With funds from a wealthy aunt and other investors, and the assistance of his younger brother Louis, he canalised a small river above the village of Auchy in northeast France and set up a water mill for spinning cotton fibre into yarn. The venture faced a recurrent technical difficulty: the parts of the wooden machine that transferred motion from the

to the spindles on which the yarn was wound repeatedly broke. Replacing the wooden parts with wrought iron failed to end the breakages, and replacing those with parts of cast iron, which is stronger but more brittle, also failed.
