Like many would-be industrialists, Say found the attempt to introduce mechanisation too much of a challenge. The wastage of material damaged in production, which amounted to 25 per cent of the raw cotton, added to the difficulties. Unable to make a profit from his hydraulic machine, Say dissolved the business in 1812 and became a rentier, investing in a number of other ventures. In particular, he helped his brother take over a sugar-refining business. A refinery was less prone to breakdowns than a textile mill, as boiling and purifying raw sugar

was a simpler process than spinning cotton fibres into fine yarns. The Louis Say Refining Company went on to become the most successful sugar business in France and one of the country’s largest industrial enterprises – although, as the firm’s manager was to discover with the fingers of his own hand, even in the refining of sugar industrial accidents could have their consequences.

zh: 与此同时，让-巴蒂斯特重新转向政治经济学；1814 年，随着拿破仑战败，他得以出版《概论》的修订版。新版与亚当·斯密和大卫·李嘉图的观点决裂——他们认为商品价值主要由生产它所需的劳动量决定——强调一个新人物企业家的同等重要贡献。这个人协调劳动和机器的使用，改进工作组织，供应或引入资本，而且最重要的是，利用他对供需原理的理解来调节生产的速度和方向——例如，决定生产棉花还是糖更有利可图。换言之，资本的“生产性作用力”之所以有效，是因为企业家身上结合了技术诀窍和经济科学。
en: Meanwhile, Jean-Baptiste turned back to political economy, and in 1814, with the defeat of Napoleon, he was able to publish a revised edition of the

. The new version broke with the view of Adam Smith and David Ricardo that the value of a good is determined principally by the amount of labour required for its production, emphasising the equally important contribution of a new figure, the entrepreneur. This person coordinates the use of labour and machines, improves the organisation of work, supplies or draws in capital, and, above all, uses his understanding of the principles of supply and demand to regulate the pace and direction of production – including, for example, deciding whether it is more profitable to produce cotton or sugar. In other words, the ‘productive agency’ of capital is effective thanks to the combining of technical know-how and economic science in the person of the entrepreneur.

zh: 一个世纪后，在二十世纪的最初几年，企业家的形象再次出现。这个人物将再一次提供托词，为资本和利息理论提供一种解释货币生钱能力的方式。随着经济学把关注点收窄为一门价格机制的科学，它发现了一种方式，可以通过企业家这个人物构成的薄弱联系，把赋予货币繁殖力的其他一切机器和生产过程重新纳入对货币本质的解释。然而，这个人物的角色被重新定义了。他不再是一位至关重要的协调者，而是被想象为偶尔的扰乱者——事实上，是一位破土者。
en: A century later, in the opening years of the twentieth century, the figure of the entrepreneur reappeared. Once again, this character would provide an alibi, offering the theory of capital and interest a way to explain the ability of money to make money. As economics narrowed its focus to become a science of the price mechanism, it would find a means to readmit into the explanation of the nature of money every other piece of machinery and process of production that gave money its reproductive power, via the tenuous human link of the entrepreneur. The role of this figure, however, was redefined. Rather than a vital coordinator, the entrepreneur was now imagined as an occasional disruptor – in fact, as a groundbreaker.

zh: 1911 年，在欧文·费雪的《利息率》问世三年后，一位年轻奥地利学者出版了他最重要的著作；此人后来迁往哈佛大学，并逐渐与费雪争夺二十世纪上半叶最有影响美国经济学家的头衔。约瑟夫·熊彼特的《经济发展理论》提出了一种关于资本和利息的论述，其中货币赚取货币的能力在决定性程度上依赖于企业家的角色。然而，对熊彼特而言，企业家不是协调者，而是失序的推动者。
企业家启动了创新、动荡和技术重组的过程，
他后来称之为“创造性破坏”。
一个多世纪后的今天，熊彼特式论述——把资本主义视为由一种独特的破坏性创新力量所驱动的过程——或许仍是对于界定资本主义现代性的那种时间经验最具说服力的解释，无论对资本权力的批评者还是捍卫者都是如此。
en: In 1911, three years after the appearance of Irving Fisher’s

, a young Austrian scholar, who would later move to Harvard University and come to rival Fisher for the title of the most influential American economist of the first half of the twentieth century, published his most important work. Joseph Schumpeter’s

proposed an account of capital and interest in which the very ability of money to earn money turned decisively on the role of the entrepreneur. For Schumpeter, however, the entrepreneur was not a coordinator but an agent of disorder.
The entrepreneur set in motion the processes of innovation, upheaval, and technical reorganisation that
he later termed ‘creative destruction’.

Today, more than a century later, the Schumpeterian account of capitalism as a process driven by a unique force of disruptive innovation remains, among critics of the power of capital as much as its defenders, perhaps the most persuasive explanation for the very experience of temporality that defines capitalist modernity.

zh: 尽管熊彼特在若干处提到让-巴蒂斯特·萨伊的著作，但把企业家角色置于货币新论述中心这一做法的动力，并非来自萨伊的《概论》，也不是来自他在维也纳求学时读到的其他文本。它来自他完成学业后的第一份工作。那份工作是在开罗。
en: While Schumpeter referred in places to the writing of Jean-Baptiste Say, the impetus for placing the role of the entrepreneur at the centre of the new account of money did not come from Say’s
, nor from other texts he encountered as a student in Vienna. It arose from his first job after completing his education. That employment was in Cairo.

zh: 熊彼特的思想是在埃及形成的，但不是通过萨伊的著作，而是通过他在那里接触到的、由让-巴蒂斯特的弟弟创建的实力雄厚的制糖企业——路易·萨伊炼糖公司。正是该公司在埃及靠糖发财的计划破产，塑造了二十世纪关于货币如何生钱的最有影响的论述。
en: Schumpeter’s ideas were formed in Egypt not by Say’s writings but in his encounter there with the powerful sugar business created by Jean-Baptiste’s brother, the Louis Say Refining Company. It was the collapse of the Company’s scheme to make a fortune from sugar in Egypt that shaped the most influential twentieth-century account of how money is made from money.

zh: 没有什么比欧洲人称之为埃及的地方，更能体现二十世纪之交“资本主义”的含义——货币生钱的权力。开罗及其乡村在 1860 年代经历了第一轮金融繁荣。政府修建铁路线，扩大棉花种植园，建立甘蔗种植园，利用美国南方奴隶种植的棉花和糖供应中断的机会，欧洲金融家推动了信用扩张，创造了“尼罗河上的克朗代克”。
然而，在美国蓄奴州战败、美国棉花出口恢复之后，棉花价格暴跌。1873 年的国际金融危机造成了进一步压力，导致埃及政府拖欠债务，落入欧洲金融控制之下。随后的一场人民起义被 1882 年英国军事占领镇压。占领为棉花和糖生产的新投资奠定了基础，到世纪之交，又创造了第二轮信用繁荣。土地本身成为投机资产，令当地观察者惊讶的是，其价值随棉花和糖价格的涨落而波动。
en: Nowhere better exemplified the sense of capitalism at the turn of the twentieth century – the power of money to make money – than the place that Europeans called Egypt. Cairo and its countryside had seen a first financial boom in the 1860s. As the government constructed railway lines, expanded cotton plantations, and established sugar cane estates, taking advantage of the interruption to the supply of slave-grown cotton and sugar from the American South, European financiers drove an expansion of credit that created a ‘Klondike on the Nile’.

However, after the defeat of the American slave states and the resumption of US cotton exports, the price paid for cotton collapsed. The international financial crisis of 1873 created further pressure and led the Egyptian government to default on its debt payments and fall under European financial control. A popular uprising that followed was ended by the British military occupation of 1882. The occupation laid the groundwork for renewed investment in cotton and sugar production, which by the turn of the century created a second credit boom. Land itself became a speculative asset, its value fluctuating, to the astonishment of local observers, with the rise and fall of the price of cotton and sugar.

zh: 到 1905 年，这个围绕棉花、糖、股票和土地投机组织起来的不断扩张的信用世界，已成为开罗政界持续辩论的话题。那年，一位主要作家雅各布·萨鲁夫在他主编的月刊
《穆克塔塔夫》的文学副刊上连载了一部小说。伊丽莎白·霍尔特认为，故事从一期到下一期的悬念，复制了这样一个世界的不确定性：在那里，富人仅仅是“从他人损失中获利的人”，“没人确知自己的明天”。
新攫取模式的物质性——其建筑、交易机制和信息系统——在印刷文化和想象生活的新形式中被复制和折射。“在欧洲各国首都，都有一座巨大的建筑，上面写着‘证券交易所’，”埃及统治精英中的一位成员 1905 年对一位法裔美国访客说，并抱怨投机者的“瘟疫”正在消耗这个国家的生命。“在这里，整个国家就是一座巨大的证券交易所。”
同年，这场繁荣的崩溃触发了 1907 年大崩盘。
en: By 1905, this expanding world of credit organised around speculation in cotton, sugar, stocks, and land became a topic of continuous debate in political circles in Cairo. A leading writer, Ya‘qub Sarruf, serialised a novel that year in a literary supplement to the monthly journal
he edited,

. The suspense from the appearance of one instalment of the story to the next replicated, Elizabeth Holt suggests, the uncertainty of a world in which the wealthy were simply ‘those who win from the loss of another’ and where ‘no one is sure of his tomorrow’.

The materiality of the new modes of capture – its buildings, exchange mechanisms, and information systems – were duplicated and refracted in new forms of print culture and imaginative life. ‘In all the capitals of Europe there is a huge building on which is written “Stock Exchange”,’ a member of Egypt’s ruling elite remarked to a French American visitor in 1905, complaining about the ‘plague’ of speculators sapping the country’s life. ‘Here the whole country is one vast Stock Exchange.’
The collapse of the boom that same year was to trigger the Great Crash of 1907.

zh: 约瑟夫·熊彼特在那场崩盘之后来到开罗，而促成此行的一连串事件，起于1905年巴黎的一起自杀。
en: The events that took Joseph Schumpeter to Cairo, in the wake of that crash, were set in motion by a suicide in Paris in 1905.

zh: 熊彼特的糖厂
en: Schumpeter’s Sugar Mill

zh: 1905 年 8 月欧内斯特·克罗尼耶之死，似乎集中体现了那些日子的金融脆弱性。一名仆人发现他的尸体躺在卧室地板上。在相邻浴室进行的尸检表明，克罗尼耶曾试图用氰化钾自杀。由于无法把毒药留在胃里，他随后朝自己的心脏开枪。
奇怪的是，他扣动扳机的那只手有两根假指，这是十二年前在他的炼糖厂检查机器维修时发生事故的结果。
那些维修，以及那些失去的手指，提供了一条我们稍后将回到的线索。
克罗尼耶被称为糖王，
，他把所控制的王国——路易·萨伊炼糖公司——建成足以垄断法国食糖市场的大型企业。他最初受聘担任工程师和经理，在路易的孙子亨利·萨伊于 1899 年去世后，接管了这家由让-巴蒂斯特及其弟弟创办的公司。
但克罗尼耶在糖期货上进行的一笔大规模投机投资失败了。接着，一封从开罗寄到巴黎的信暗示，他在那里对所控制的制糖业的欺诈性经营——曾为投机提供资金——已被发现。几天之内，他结束了自己的生命。
1905 年 8 月 27 日他去世的消息传出后，公司股价暴跌。巴黎股市下挫，造成巨额损失，随后的几天，伦敦、纽约和汉堡交易所的交易商也感受到了这场
冲击。
en: The death of Ernest Cronier in August 1905 seemed to epitomise the financial fragility of those days. A servant found his body on the bedroom floor. The autopsy, carried out in the adjoining bathroom, revealed that Cronier had tried to poison himself with potassium cyanide. Unable to keep the poison down, he then shot himself in the heart.
Curiously, the hand with which he pulled the trigger had two prosthetic fingers, the consequence of an accident twelve years earlier inspecting repairs to machinery at his sugar refinery.
Those repairs, and the missing fingers, provide a clue to which we will return.
Known as the sugar king,

, Cronier had built the kingdom he controlled, the Louis Say Refining Company, into a business large enough to corner the French sugar market. Hired first as an engineer and manager, he had taken control of the firm – founded by Jean-Baptiste and his brother Louis – following the death of Louis’s grandson, Henri Say, in 1899.

But a large speculative investment Cronier had made in sugar futures had failed. Then a letter reached him in Paris from Cairo suggesting that his fraudulent management of the sugar industry he controlled there, which had funded the speculation, had been uncovered. Within days, he took his life.
On the news of his death, on 27 August 1905, the value of the Company’s shares collapsed. The Paris stock market fell, causing huge losses, and traders felt the
shock over the following days in the exchanges of London, New York, and Hamburg.

zh: 在亚历山大和开罗——当时那里的货币市场属于世界上最活跃之列——冲击更大。路易·萨伊炼糖公司不久前才与当地投资者以及我们先前遇到的英国金融家欧内斯特·卡塞尔爵士合伙，控制了埃及制糖业，创建了这个国家最大的工业企业。该公司前景一度未卜。世纪之交阿斯旺大坝的完工，导致农民出人意料地减少而非扩大甘蔗种植。这家公司没有从加工甘蔗中获利，反而成了一家生产债务的企业。它的董事们靠发行没有真实销售基础的虚构汇票而兴旺，创造出为克罗尼耶在巴黎进行糖期货投机提供资金的信用货币。经理的自杀迫使这家埃及公司暂停交易其暴跌的股票并进行重组，关闭一半炼糖厂，出售甘蔗种植园和农业铁路。
en: In Alexandria and Cairo, where the money markets were among the most active in the world at that time, the shock was even greater. The Louis Say Refining Company had only recently taken control of the Egyptian sugar industry, in partnership with local investors and Sir Ernest Cassel, the British financier we met earlier, creating the country’s largest industrial enterprise. The firm had faced an uncertain future. The completion of the Aswan Dam at the turn of the century had led farmers unexpectedly to decrease rather than expand the growing of sugar cane. Instead of profiting from processing the cane, the firm had become a business for producing debt. Its directors had prospered by issuing fictitious bills of exchange, with no underlying sale, creating the credit money that funded Cronier’s speculations in sugar futures in Paris. The manager’s suicide forced the Egyptian company to suspend dealing in its collapsing shares and reorganise, closing half its refineries and selling off its sugar estates and agricultural railways.

zh: 反常的是，这场抛售助长了埃及殖民未来的新一轮投机，制造了一场繁荣；十八个月后，即 1907 年 4 月，这场繁荣的崩溃震动了全世界。在这十八个月里，买家抬高农业土地开发公司的价格，房地产公司在开罗和亚历山大推动了一股建设狂热，组织债务创造的银行和抵押贷款公司也是如此。
“人们显然疯了，”后来提交给埃及国民银行股东的一份报告说，这家金融机构正是卡塞尔帮助创建的。“他们似乎认为，每一家新成立的公司，甚至在开始营业之前，价值就已经翻倍。”
en: Perversely, the sell-off fuelled a new round of speculation in Egypt’s colonial future, creating a boom whose collapse eighteen months later, in April 1907, was to reverberate around the world. Over those eighteen months, buyers bid up the price of agrarian land development companies, and property firms promoted a frenzy of construction in Cairo and Alexandria, as did the banks and mortgage companies organising the creation of debt.

‘People were apparently mad,’ according to a later report to the shareholders of the National Bank of Egypt, the financial firm that Cassel had helped create. ‘They seemed to think that every company that came out was worth double its value even before it had started business.’

zh: 然而突然间，英国对埃及殖民占领的长期未来——一个与阿斯旺大坝一起造就了那些股票和抵押贷款价值的政治未来——似乎不那么确定了。1906 年夏天，反对英国占领的抗议加剧；此前在开罗以北四十五英里的三角洲村庄丁沙瓦伊，村民反抗英国士兵为取乐射杀他们的家鸽（家鸽养在鸽舍里，用于收集鸽粪作肥料；在新的灌溉方案对土壤肥力造成有害影响后，这些养分变得日益重要），随后四人被绞死，其他人被监禁和鞭打，公众对此予以谴责。为了减少政治反对，次年 4 月，伦敦政府接受了其驻开罗总督
克罗默勋爵的辞呈；克罗默自 1883 年起管理殖民政府。
en: Suddenly, however, the long-term future of Britain’s colonial occupation of Egypt, a political future that had, along with the dam, produced the value of those shares and mortgages, seemed less certain. In the summer of 1906, protests against the British occupation intensified, in public condemnation of the hanging of four men and the imprisonment and flogging of others in the Delta village of Dinshawai, forty-five miles north of Cairo, after they resisted British soldiers shooting their domestic pigeons for sport (housed in dovecotes, pigeons were raised for their droppings, which were used as fertiliser, providing nutrients of increasing importance following the deleterious effect of the new irrigation schemes on soil fertility). Anxious to reduce political opposition, the following April the government in London accepted the resignation
of its proconsul in Cairo, Lord Cromer, who had administered the colonial government since 1883.

zh: 随后，一场自 1 月起威胁就已显而易见的金融危机爆发了。从伦敦紧急运送的 60 万英镑黄金未能阻止银行挤兑。“埃及最先倒下，”当时对 1907 年全球金融危机最具说服力的记述报道说。
恐慌蔓延到日本、德国和智利，然后在 10 月蔓延到纽约；华尔街的崩溃引发了一场金融收缩，其严重程度在此后一个世纪中只有大萧条超过。
en: A financial crisis, the threat of which had been clear since January, then broke. An emergency shipment of £600,000 in gold from London failed to stop the run on the banks. ‘Egypt went first’, the most persuasive contemporary account of the worldwide financial crisis of 1907 reported.

The panic spread to Japan, Germany, and Chile, and then by October to New York, where the collapse on Wall Street triggered a financial contraction, whose severity was surpassed over the next century only by the Great Depression.

zh: 与此同时，埃及法院任命了一组专家来重组这家糖业公司。他们的计划是扩大当地甘蔗的加工，而不是试图从加工进口的受补贴奥地利甜菜糖中获利。为协助重组，负责人聘请了一位年轻的奥地利律师——未来的哈佛经济学家约瑟夫·熊彼特。熊彼特受过经济学训练（当时欧洲大学仍把经济学作为法律的一个分支教授），1908 年大部分时间都在开罗度过，并在业余时间发展了那本书的构思；回到欧洲后不久，他便完成了写作。
en: Meanwhile, the Egyptian courts had appointed a group of experts to reorganise the sugar company. Their plan was to expand the refining of local sugar cane, rather than trying to profit from processing imports of subsidised Austrian beet sugar. To assist in the reorganisation, those in charge hired a young Austrian lawyer – the future Harvard economist Joseph Schumpeter. Trained in economics (still taught as a branch of law in European universities at that time), Schumpeter spent most of 1908 in Cairo, and in his spare time developed the ideas for the book that he completed writing soon after his return to Europe.

zh: 熊彼特的《经济发展理论》探讨了如何解释这个不断扩张的货币生钱世界。这个问题再次被提为资本如何赚取利息的问题。他希望理解他所说的“抽吸装置”；这种装置使资本家——即信用的提供者——能够从利润中抽出“源源不断的商品流”。
为解释这套装置，这本书吸收了他重组糖业企业时获得的洞见。他的传记作者指出，在开罗，熊彼特“获得了实际的商业经验，以及商业和贸易在现实世界中如何运作的第一手知识”，他帮助重组糖业公司，实施不同的生产方法。“他对这项创新的参与给熊彼特留下了不可磨灭的印象。他亲眼见证了创新过程及其后果。这后来成为他理论的核心。”
正如现代证券交易所为上一代经济学家提供了一个简化场所，使他们得以从中推导价格机制的抽象模型，一次对殖民埃及制糖业的短暂接触，也为熊彼特提供了实验室，让他以企业家的形象生成一整套资本理论。
en: Schumpeter’s

addressed the question of how to explain this expanding world of money that makes money. The question was posed, once again, as the issue of how capital earns interest. He wished to understand what he called ‘the suction apparatus’ that enabled the capitalist, meaning the supplier of credit, to draw ‘a permanent stream of goods from profits’.

To explain the apparatus, the book drew on insights he obtained while reorganising the sugar business. In Cairo, his biographer notes, Schumpeter ‘acquired practical business experience and firsthand knowledge of how business and commerce worked in the real world’, in helping to reorganise the sugar company and implement different methods of production. ‘His participation in this innovation made an indelible impression on Schumpeter. He had witnessed firsthand the innovation process and its consequences. It would later become a centrepiece for his theory.’

Just as the modern stock exchange had provided a previous generation of economists with a simplified site from which to derive an abstract model of the price mechanism, a brief encounter with the business of sugar production in colonial Egypt provided Schumpeter with the laboratory in which to generate, in the figure of the entrepreneur, an entire theory of capital.

zh: 这本书具有广泛影响的论点是，货币扩张
的力量——换言之，资本家通过创造信用赚取利息的能力——并非来自货币的属性，也非来自提供货币的资本家的权力，而是来自另一个不同人物——企业家——的独特角色。企业家的作用不是像萨伊所主张的那样协调商业，而是扰乱商业。
en: The widely influential argument of the book was that the power of

money to expand – the ability, in other words, of the capitalist to earn interest from the creation of credit – arose not from the properties of money, nor from the powers of the capitalist who supplied it, but from the distinctive role of a different figure, the entrepreneur. The role of the entrepreneur was not to coordinate business, as Say had argued, but to disrupt it.

zh: 利息作为对扰乱的回报
en: Interest as a Reward for Disruption

zh: 瓦尔拉斯和费雪等人设计的经济生活模型基于均衡原理，假定市场价格机制会不断在商品需求与供给之间产生平衡；这些模型没有给蓄意扰乱留出位置。因此，这些经济学家无法解释货币的赚钱能力，除非假定一种普遍的“时间偏好”，即偏好当下商品甚于未来商品。他们推测，这种偏好使那些向急需某种商品的借款人提供信用货币的人，能够索取一笔溢价（利息收费），迫使那些不愿等待的人支付超过商品价值的费用。正如熊彼特所指出的，这种普遍偏好没有证据。大多数企业通过留存利润为其持续或扩张活动提供资金，无需为使用货币支付费用（正如今天，股票市场在为企业提供资本方面作用极小）。
只有那些陷入困境的人，例如面临财产被剥夺的债务人或面临意外危机的企业，才被迫以利息借入货币。要解释货币利息支付近来已成为普遍特征这一事实，就必须理解企业家的角色。
en: The models of economic life that men like Walras and Fisher devised, based on the principle of equilibrium, where the mechanism of a market price is assumed to continually produce a balance between the demand for goods and their supply, had no place for deliberate disruption. These economists were therefore unable to account for the earning power of money, except by positing a universal ‘time preference’ for present over future goods. This preference, they surmised, allowed those supplying credit money to a borrower seeking a good immediately to exact a premium (an interest charge), forcing those unwilling to wait for a good to pay more than its value. As Schumpeter pointed out, there was no evidence for this universal preference. Most businesses funded their continuing or expanding activities through retained profits, with no need to pay a fee for the use of money (just as today, stock markets played very little role in providing capital for business firms).

Only those in distress, such as a debtor facing dispossession or a business facing an unexpected crisis, were forced to borrow money at interest. To explain the fact that the payment of interest on money had recently become a general feature, one had to understand the role of the entrepreneur.

zh: 熊彼特写道，企业家是引入“新组合”的人，这些组合重组了现有的生产过程。重新安排使一家企业短暂地比竞争对手更有利可图。这种持续的重组在整个工业生活中反复进行，使经济生活的均衡论述所设想的、生产与消费之间的商品循环流动反复受到扰乱。扰乱产生了动态运动。与趋于均衡的经济过程这一形象相对照，熊彼特把这种扰乱性运动称为经济“发展”。他的论述不仅仅是对资本主义制度运作的社会学解释。它是对资本赚取利息、货币累积货币之力量这一解释难题的一种
解答。企业家区别于普通企业经营者之处在于，作为创新者，企业家是唯一无法从留存收益或预期收益中为经营提供资金的行动者。看重当下资金之获取甚于未来货币，并不是普遍的人类特征；它源于企业家的特殊需要，企业家必须作为债务人运作。这种需要确立了一个货币市场，其价格就是利率。不同领域企业家对货币的需求，被市场转化为适用于一切资本的普遍利率。
en: Entrepreneurs are those who introduce ‘new combinations’, Schumpeter wrote, which reorganise an existing productive process. The rearrangement makes a business briefly more profitable than its rivals. Carried out repeatedly across the whole of industrial life, this continual rearranging causes the circular flow of goods between production and consumption, as envisioned in the equilibrium account of economic life, to be repeatedly disrupted. The disruption gives rise to a dynamic movement. As a contrast with the image of economic processes tending towards an equilibrium, Schumpeter termed this disruptive movement economic ‘development’. His account was not just a sociological explanation for the working of a capitalist system. It was a

solution to the problem of explaining the power of capital to earn interest, of money to accumulate money. What distinguished the entrepreneur from the ordinary operator of a business was that, as an innovator, the entrepreneur was the only agent unable to fund operations out of retained or expected earnings. Valuing the access to present funds over future money was not a general human trait; it arose from the special needs of the entrepreneur, who was required to operate as a debtor. This need established a market for money, for which the price was the rate of interest. The demand for money among entrepreneurs in different fields was transformed by the market into the general rate of interest for all capital.

zh: 对熊彼特而言，利息不是货币的内在属性，也不是对耐心的回报。它只是企业家赚取的一种特殊利润，作为重组生产过程的临时回报。重新安排使一家企业短暂地比竞争对手更有利可图。一旦其他企业采用同样的方法，竞争就会压低商品价格，企业家的利润也就终结。为说明这个过程，他举了一个直接来自开罗经验的例子。“让我们假设一位先前种植甘蔗的种植者改种棉花，而棉花直到不久前还比现在更有利可图。这是一种新组合；此人因此成为企业家并赚取利润。”接着，竞争压低收入，例如通过增加地租——“正如实际发生的那样”，他写道——到那时，“这个人的企业家职能便消失了”。
en: For Schumpeter, interest was not an intrinsic property of money, nor a reward for patience. Rather, it was simply the special kind of profit earned by an entrepreneur, as a temporary reward for reorganising a process of production. The rearrangement briefly makes an enterprise more profitable than its rivals. As soon as other businesses adopt the same methods, competition forces down the prices of goods and the entrepreneur’s profit comes to an end. To illustrate this process, he gave an example drawn directly from his own experience in Cairo. ‘Let us assume that a planter who has previously cultivated sugar cane changes over to cotton-growing, which until recently was more lucrative than it is now. This is a new combination; the man thereby becomes an entrepreneur and makes a profit.’ Then, competition forces down receipts, for example through an increase in the rent of the land – ‘as has actually happened’, he notes – and at that point ‘the entrepreneurial function of this man disappears’.

zh: 让-巴蒂斯特·萨伊曾尝试棉花制造，失败后与弟弟合作实施一项更简单的炼糖计划，从而偶然发现了企业家的重要性。熊彼特也通过描述一位种植者把种植从棉花转向甘蔗，以同样的材料获得了类似的启示。而且他是在拯救同一家法国糖业公司时做到这一点的。
en: Jean-Baptiste Say had chanced upon the importance of the entrepreneur by trying his hand at cotton manufacturing, failing, and then collaborating with his brother on a simpler scheme for refining sugar. Schumpeter had had a similar revelation, with the same materials, by describing a plantation owner who shifts their cultivation from cotton to sugar cane. And he did it while rescuing the same French sugar company.
body.review: 校注：上一段所引熊彼特例子是从甘蔗改种棉花，本段原文却写从棉花改种甘蔗，改种方向前后不一。译文保留原作差异。

zh: 在开罗期间，熊彼特可能亲身经历了种植甘蔗还是改种棉花这一选择。除了拯救糖业公司，他还参与组织了一座新的农业庄园，它属于埃及统治家族的一位公主。资料没有告诉我们这个人的名字。然而，这很可能是与赫迪夫分居的妻子；她像熊彼特一样是奥地利人，最近在开罗北郊获得了自己的宫殿和庄园。她通过
她的兄弟结识了赫迪夫；她的兄弟曾是赫迪夫在维也纳特蕾西亚学院的同班同学，哈布斯堡帝国的政治精英在那里接受教育，几位奥斯曼—埃及王子也被送到那里学习。熊彼特是同一所学校的毕业生。熊彼特喜欢回忆商业成功之外的其他成就，并习惯于“凭魅力与年轻女性亲近”；他后来吹嘘自己与这位公主有染。

与任何私人关系相比，有趣却从未被提及的是熊彼特所参与的那家企业的性质。这座庄园位于开罗北郊的穆斯塔鲁德（今天是埃及最大炼油厂的所在地），对于当时在那里涌现的企业家形式而言，既典型又不寻常。它建在五年前阿斯旺大坝完工后才得以开放、可进行夏季棉花种植的土地上。它属于赫迪夫最近购置的一组示范农场，包括邻近的一座他自己的庄园，用于试验扩大棉花种植。一位英国作家刚在一本书中详细描述了这一模式，该书旨在鼓励“有意在这个受眷顾的国度从事商业生涯”的英国定居者迁往埃及，购地开发为棉花种植园。
en: While in Cairo, Schumpeter may have experienced exactly this choice between planting sugar cane or switching to the cultivation of cotton. Besides rescuing the sugar company, he also had a hand in the organisation of a new agricultural estate, belonging to a princess of the Egyptian ruling family. The sources do not tell us the name of the person. However, this was likely the estranged wife of the Khedive, an Austrian like Schumpeter, who had recently acquired her own palace and estate on the northern outskirts of Cairo. She had met the Khedive

through her brother, who had been his classmate at the Theresianum in Vienna, where the political elite of the Habsburg Empire was educated and where several Ottoman-Egyptian princes were sent to study. Schumpeter was a graduate of the same school. Fond of recalling other achievements besides his business success, and in the habit of ‘charm[ing] his way into intimacies with young women’, Schumpeter later boasted of having an affair with the princess.

Rather than any personal liaison, what is interesting but never mentioned is the nature of the enterprise in which Schumpeter had a hand. Located at Mostorod, on the northern outskirts of Cairo (today the site of Egypt’s largest oil refinery), the estate was both typical and unusual for the forms of entrepreneurship emerging there at that moment. It was built on lands made open to the summer cultivation of cotton by the completion five years earlier of the Aswan Dam. It formed part of a group of model farms that the Khedive had recently acquired, including a neighbouring estate of his own, to experiment in the expansion of cotton cultivation. An English writer had just described the model in detail, in a book aimed at encouraging English settlers ‘disposed to enter upon a business career in this favoured country’ to move to Egypt and buy up land to develop as cotton plantations.

zh: 在繁荣的开罗城短暂而多事的逗留期间，熊彼特相信，他通过自己对企业家的短暂体验，发现了资本主义与未来独特关系的秘密。
然而，企业家在此出现，并不是作为资本主义的动力之钥，而是作为帮助召唤出其托词的人。
en: In his short and eventful stay in the booming city of Cairo, Schumpeter believed he had discovered, through his own brief experience of the role of the entrepreneur, the secret of capitalism’s distinctive relationship to the future.
The entrepreneur makes his appearance here, however, not as the key to the dynamic of capitalism, but as the one who helps to conjure into being its alibi.

zh: 资本的托词出现在这种既显得具有开创性、又显得是增长来源的组合之中。如果资本获得了它那种神秘的扩张能力，使货币能够生钱，那么就要在一种被误认为创新的破坏性力量中提供解释。为了命名他对资本主义的理解——一个以这种新的货币力量为特征的体系——熊彼特在书名中提出了一个新词：“经济发展”（
）。发展，即引入新组合，是由企业家触发的过程。把所谓新古典经济理论所研究的静态循环交换过程，与动态的商业过程、或货币具有扩张性赚钱能力的资本主义体系区分开来，正取决于这个新出现的“发展”概念。
en: The alibi of capital emerges in this combination of what appears as both groundbreaking and the source of growth. If capital has acquired its mysterious ability to expand, enabling money to make money, an explanation is to be offered in the disruptive force misrecognised as innovation. To name his understanding of capitalism, as a system characterised by this new power of money, Schumpeter presented in the title of his book a novel term: ‘economic development’ (

). Development, or the introduction of new combinations, was the process triggered by the entrepreneur. Distinguishing the static, circular process of exchange studied by so-called neoclassical economic theory from the dynamic process of business, or the capitalist system in which money had an expanding power to make money, depended on this emergent concept of development.

zh: 熊彼特书名中的“经济发展”一词，尚未
具有它在此后几十年将获得的更广泛含义。到二十世纪中叶，正如我们将在
看到的，经济的发明——一个以其“增长”来构想和衡量的对象——将改变发展的含义。在世纪之交的开罗，英国殖民政权还没有经济发展的概念。这不是他们使用的术语。他们专注于发展，但他们使用这个词时有更早、更具体的含义——它不指经济的发展，甚至也不指更含糊的经济发展（他们不使用这个术语），而是指“土地开发”。
它描述了当时英国政策的重点：尼罗河的重组、灌溉工程的扩张，以及把农业转变为大规模私人和公司债务创造的领域。这正是熊彼特从中抽象出其资本理论的过程：把土地转为更有利可图的用途，或者说，由于灌溉方案以及棉花和甘蔗等工业作物的传播，转为更容易被资本化的用途。土地被重塑为一台更强大的装置，用于从未来“抽吸”收入。
en: The term ‘economic development’ in Schumpeter’s title did not yet
have the wider meaning it would acquire in subsequent decades. By the mid-twentieth century, as we will see in

, the invention of the economy, an object conceived and measured in terms of its ‘growth’, would transform the meaning of development. In turn-of-the-century Cairo, the British colonial regime had as yet no conception of economic development. It was not a term they used. They were preoccupied with development, but their use of the word had an earlier and more specific sense – it referred not to the development of an economy, nor even to a vaguer economic development, a term they did not use, but to ‘land development’.

It described the focus of British policy at that time, the reorganisation of the Nile, the expansion of irrigation works, and the transformation of agriculture into a field of extensive private and corporate debt creation. This was precisely the process from which Schumpeter abstracted his theory of capital: converting land to more profitable purposes, or rather to purposes more easily capitalised, thanks to irrigation schemes and the spread of industrial crops such as cotton and sugar cane. Land was remade as a more powerful apparatus for the ‘suction’ of income from the future.

zh: 种植棉花或甘蔗，以及决定从一种改种另一种，并没有什么创新之处。正如我们很快将会看到，两者在尼罗河谷的种植都已超过一千年。它们与增长也没有任何简单关系，因为这两种作物的产量都将下降。
我们在此引入这些农业计划，是为了追问它们所设计的新未来关系，同时避免暗示这代表了“改良”，或“增长”或“发展”的普遍过程。要把握对资本主义条件下未来工程的一种不同理解，出发点是用以下问题取代把历史构想为经济发展的做法：对未来收入的控制是如何被工程化的，未来本身又是如何通过组织耐久性与流动性的组合，被生产为集体生活的框架的。
en: There was nothing innovative about the cultivating of cotton or sugar cane, or the decision to switch from one to another. Both had been cultivated in the Nile Valley, as we shall shortly see, for more than a millennium. Nor did they have any simple relationship to growth, since the yields of both crops were set to decline.

In introducing here these agricultural schemes, our aim has been to ask about the new relationship to the future that they engineered, while avoiding the implication that this represented ‘improvement’ or a general process of ‘growth’ or ‘development’. To grasp a different understanding of the engineering of the future under capitalism, the starting point is to replace a history conceived as economic development with the question of how the control of future revenues is engineered, and how the future itself is produced as a frame of collective life, through organising combinations of the durable and the liquid.

zh: 熊彼特的埃及糖厂使我们能够把本书已开始追问的几个问题连接起来。在帝国时代——大致指第一次世界大战之前帝国迅速扩张的五十年——同时发生了两件事：技术圈的迅速扩张加速了对大地的破坏；经济学家和其他人用来解释非凡财富攫取——这种攫取
伴随着这场对大地的攻击——的观点和思想，也同时呈现出轻盈或转瞬即逝的性质。破土活动在尘世间的物质破坏性，似乎与企业家的非物质性、观念性、想象性工作截然相反——尽管在实践中两者不可分割。破土使大规模从未来抽取成为可能，并在此过程中产生了不稳定性和不确定性；这些不稳定性和不确定性集中体现在新人物“破土者”——即“资本家”——身上。
en: Schumpeter’s Egyptian sugar mill allows us to connect together several questions that this book has begun to ask. In the age of empire, meaning roughly the five decades of rapid imperial expansion prior to the First World War, there occurred both an accelerated breaking of the Earth, in the rapid expansion of the technosphere, and a simultaneous lightness or evanescence of the arguments and ideas with which economists and others tried to explain the extraordinary capture of wealth that

accompanied this ground assault. The earthly, material destructiveness of the groundbreaking appeared as the very opposite of the immaterial, ideational, imaginative work of the entrepreneur – although in practice the two were inseparable. Groundbreaking made it possible to extract from the future on a large scale, and in the process to generate instabilities and uncertainties personified in the new figure of the ground-breaker, the ‘capitalist’.

zh: 熊彼特和妻子在开罗都染上了一种严重的发热病，导致他们在不到一年后便缩短了在该国的逗留。下一章，我们将在埃及多停留一段时间。离开糖厂大门和示范农场之后，是时候展开更广泛的问题：资本主义与未来的关系，以及现代货币的力量，是如何被组织起来的。我们将看到，种植棉花还是甘蔗的选择，并不仅仅是企业家的进取决定。为了产生企业家及其决定，整个国家必须被重塑，其生态必须被重新工程化，其人民必须被贫困化，其河流必须被毁灭。
en: Schumpeter and his wife both contracted a serious fever while in Cairo, causing them to cut short their stay in the country after less than a year. In the next chapter, we will linger in Egypt a little longer. Leaving the gates of the sugar factory and the model farm, it is time to open up wider questions about how the capitalist relationship to the future, and the modern power of money, were organised. As we will see, the choice between growing cotton and sugar cane was not simply the enterprising decision of an entrepreneur. To produce the entrepreneur and his decision, an entire country had to be remade, its ecology re-engineered, its people impoverished, and its river destroyed.
